questions.question: If \(\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \dots, \mathbf{v}_6\) are six vectors in \(\mathbb{R}^4\), which one of the following statements is FALSE?
options: It is not necessary that these vectors span \(\mathbb{R}^4\).
These vectors are not linearly independent.
Any four of these vectors form a basis for \(\mathbb{R}^4\).
If \(\{\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_3, \mathbf{v}_5, \mathbf{v}_6\}\) spans \(\mathbb{R}^4\), then it forms a basis for \(\mathbb{R}^4\).
questions.explanation:
Given six vectors \(\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \dots, \mathbf{v}_6\) in \(\mathbb{R}^4\).
  • Statement (A): It is not necessary that these vectors span \(\mathbb{R}^4\). This is TRUE. While the minimum number of vectors needed to span \(\mathbb{R}^4\) is 4, having 6 vectors does not guarantee a span if they are linearly dependent (e.g., all 6 could lie on a single line).
  • Statement (B): These vectors are not linearly independent. This is TRUE. In a vector space of dimension \(n\), any set containing more than \(n\) vectors must be linearly dependent. Since \(6 > 4\), the set is definitely linearly dependent.
  • Statement (C): Any four of these vectors form a basis for \(\mathbb{R}^4\). This is FALSE. For four vectors to form a basis for \(\mathbb{R}^4\), they must be linearly independent. There is no guarantee that any subset of four vectors from the given six will be linearly independent (e.g., some could be zero vectors or multiples of others).
  • Statement (D): If \(\{\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_3, \mathbf{v}_5, \mathbf{v}_6\}\) spans \(\mathbb{R}^4\), then it forms a basis for \(\mathbb{R}^4\). This is TRUE. In an \(n\)-dimensional space, a set of \(n\) vectors that spans the space is automatically a basis.
The false statement is (C). \[\boxed{\text{(C) Any four of these vectors form a basis for $\mathbb{R}^4$.}}\]
Key points
  • Basis Dimension: A basis for \(\mathbb{R}^n\) must contain exactly \(n\) linearly independent vectors.
  • Linear Dependence: Any set of \(m\) vectors in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) where \(m > n\) is linearly dependent.
  • Spanning Set: A set of \(n\) vectors in an \(n\)-dimensional space forms a basis if and only if it spans the space.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not assume that having "enough" vectors (4 or more) automatically guarantees they span \(\mathbb{R}^4\) or contain a basis.
  • Remember that linear independence is a requirement for a basis, not just the count of vectors.

questions.question:
Consider the following system of linear equations. \[\begin{gathered}
  x_1 + 2x_2 = b_1; \quad 2x_1 + 4x_2 = b_2; \\
  3x_1 + 7x_2 = b_3; \quad 3x_1 + 9x_2 = b_4
\end{gathered}\] Which one of the following conditions ensures that a solution exists for the above system?
questions.explanation:
Consider the augmented matrix \((A \mid B)\) for the given system of linear equations: \[(A \mid B) = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 
1 & 2 & b_1 \\ 
2 & 4 & b_2 \\ 
3 & 7 & b_3 \\ 
3 & 9 & b_4 
\end{array} \right]\] Applying row operations \(R_2 \to R_2 - 2R_1\), \(R_3 \to R_3 - 3R_1\), and \(R_4 \to R_4 - 3R_1\): \[\Rightarrow (A \mid B) \sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 
1 & 2 & b_1 \\ 
0 & 0 & b_2 - 2b_1 \\ 
0 & 1 & b_3 - 3b_1 \\ 
0 & 3 & b_4 - 3b_1 
\end{array} \right]\] Interchanging rows \(R_2 \leftrightarrow R_3\): \[\Rightarrow (A \mid B) \sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 
1 & 2 & b_1 \\ 
0 & 1 & b_3 - 3b_1 \\ 
0 & 0 & b_2 - 2b_1 \\ 
0 & 3 & b_4 - 3b_1 
\end{array} \right]\] Applying row operation \(R_4 \to R_4 - 3R_2\): \[\Rightarrow (A \mid B) \sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 
1 & 2 & b_1 \\ 
0 & 1 & b_3 - 3b_1 \\ 
0 & 0 & b_2 - 2b_1 \\ 
0 & 0 & 6b_1 - 3b_3 + b_4 
\end{array} \right]\] Here, \(\rho(A) = 2\). To have a solution, \(\rho(A) = \rho(A \mid B)\). \[b_2 - 2b_1 = 0 \implies b_2 = 2b_1\] \[6b_1 - 3b_3 + b_4 = 0\] Thus, the system has a solution if \(b_2 = 2b_1\) and \(6b_1 - 3b_3 + b_4 = 0\). \[\boxed{\text{(A) $b_2 = 2b_1$ and $6b_1 - 3b_3 + b_4 = 0$}}\]

questions.question: For the solid \(S\) shown below, the value of \(\iiint\limits_{s}x dxdydz\) (rounded off to two decimal places) is
questions.explanation:
From the figures, the limits of the integral are given by \[\text{Limits : } \begin{cases} x = 0 \text{ to } x = 3 \\ y = 0 \text{ to } y = 1 \\ z = 0 \text{ to } z = 1 - y \end{cases}\] The integral \(I\) is evaluated as: \[I = \int_{x=0}^{3} \left[ \int_{y=0}^{1} \left( \int_{z=0}^{1-y} x dz \right) dy \right] dx\] \[= \int_{x=0}^{3} \left[ \int_{y=0}^{1} [x(z)]_{0}^{1-y} dy \right] dx\] \[= \int_{x=0}^{3} \left[ \int_{y=0}^{1} x(1 - y) dy \right] dx\] \[= \left( \frac{x^2}{2} \right)_{0}^{3} \cdot \left( y - \frac{y^2}{2} \right)_{0}^{1}\] \[= \frac{9}{2} \cdot \left( 1 - \frac{1}{2} \right)\] \[= \frac{9}{4} = 2.25\] \[\boxed{2.25}\]
Key points
  • For a solid region, identify the projection on a coordinate plane (e.g., \(yz\)-plane) to find the limits for two variables.
  • The third variable's limits are determined by the surfaces bounding the solid in that direction.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Ensure the order of integration \(dz\,dy\,dx\) matches the dependency of the limits; outer limits must always be constants.
  • Do not confuse the surface \(z + y = 1\) with a constant limit for \(z\) if \(y\) is still being integrated.

questions.question:
The partial derivative of the following function
\(f(x, y, z) = e^{1-x\cos y} + xz e^{-\frac{1}{(1+y^2)}}\) With respect to \(x\) at the point \((1, 0, e)\) is
questions.explanation:
Given \(f(x, y, z) = e^{1-x \cos y} + x z e^{-\frac{1}{(1+y^2)}}\) and \((x, y, z) = (1, 0, e)\). Calculating the partial derivative with respect to \(x\): \[f_x = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} = e^{1-x \cos y} (-\cos y) + z e^{-\frac{1}{1+y^2}}\] Substituting the point \((1, 0, e)\): \[\therefore (f_x)_{(1,0,e)} = e^{1-1}(-\cos 0) + (e) e^{-\frac{1}{1+0}}\] \[= e^0(-1) + e \cdot e^{-1}\] \[= -1 + 1 = 0\] \[\boxed{\text{(b)}\ \ 0}\]
Key points
  • Partial Differentiation: When differentiating with respect to \(x\), all other variables (\(y\) and \(z\)) are treated as constants.
  • Chain Rule: \(\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(e^{u(x)}) = e^{u(x)} \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\).

questions.question: The partial derivative of the function \[f(x,y,z) = e^{1-x\,\cos{y}} + xze^{-1/\bigl(1 + y^2\bigr)}\] with respect to \(x\) at the point \((1,0,e)\) is
questions.explanation:
Given function is \[f(x,y,z) = e^{\,1-x\cos y} + xze^{-1/(1+y^2)}\] Partially differentiating with respect to \(x\), \[\frac{\partial f}{\partial x} = e^{\,1-x\cos y}(-\cos y) + ze^{-1/(1+y^2)}\] At the point \((1,0,e),\ \cos 0 = 1\) Hence, \[\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\Bigg|_{(1,0,e)} = \bigl[e^{\,1-1}(-1)\bigr] + \bigl[e\cdot e^{-1}\bigr] = -1+1 = 0\] \[\boxed{\text{(B)}\ 0}\]
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not substitute the point \((1,0,e)\) before computing the partial derivative

questions.question: The general solution of \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 6\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 9y = 0\) is
questions.explanation:
Given differential equation is \[\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} - 6\frac{dy}{dt} + 9y = 0\] Replacing \(\dfrac{d}{dt}\) by \(D\), \[(D^2 - 6D + 9)y = 0\] The auxiliary equation is \[m^2 - 6m + 9 = 0\] \[(m-3)^2 = 0\] Hence, the roots are repeated:\(m = 3,3\) For equal repeated roots \(m=a\), the complementary function is \[y = (C_1 + C_2x)e^{ax}\] Substituting \(a=3\), \[y = (C_1 + C_2x)e^{3x}\] \[\boxed{\text{(C)}\ y = (C_1 + C_2x)e^{3x}}\]
Key points
  • A homogeneous differential equation has only the complementary function as its general solution.

questions.question: Which one of the following options contain two solutions of the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (y-1)x\) ?
questions.explanation:
Given differential equation is \[\frac{dy}{dx} = (y-1)x\] Case-1: For \(y\neq 1\), separate the variables: \[\frac{dy}{y-1}=x\,dx\] Integrating both sides, \[\int \frac{dy}{y-1} = \int x\,dx\] \[\ln|y-1| = \frac{x^2}{2}+C\] \[\ln|y-1| = 0.5x^2+C\] Case-2: Check for constant solutions. If \(y=1, \frac{dy}{dx} = 0\) Substituting into the differential equation, \[0 = (1-1)x = 0\] \[y = 1\] Therefore, the two solutions are \[\ln|y-1| = 0.5x^2 + C \quad \text{and} \quad y = 1\] \[\boxed{\text{(A)}\ \ln|y-1| = 0.5x^2 + C\ \text{and}\ y = 1}\]
Mistakes to avoid
  • Constant solutions may be lost during division and must be checked separately.

questions.question: The two sides of a fair coin are labelled as 0 and 1. The coin is tossed two times independently. Let \(M\) and \(N\) denote the labels corresponding to the outcomes of those tosses. For a random variable \(X\), defined as \(X = min(M,N)\), the expected value of \(E(X)\) (rounded off to two decimal places) is .
questions.explanation:
A fair coin has sides labelled \(0\) and \(1\). The coin is tossed twice independently. Given: \[M = \text{outcome of first toss}\] \[N = \text{outcome of second toss}\] The random variable is defined as \[X = \min(M,N)\] Possible outcomes are: \[\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
(M,N) & X=\min(M,N) & \text{Probability} \\
\hline
(1,1) & 1 & \frac{1}{4} \\ (1,0) & 0 & \frac{1}{4} \\ (0,1) & 0 & \frac{1}{4} \\ (0,0) & 0 & \frac{1}{4} \\
\hline
\end{array}\] Hence, \[P(X=1)=\frac{1}{4}, \qquad P(X=0)=\frac{3}{4}\] The expectation is \(E[X]=\sum xP(x)\) Therefore, \[E[X] = \left(1\times\frac{1}{4}\right) + \left(0\times\frac{3}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{4} = 0.25\] \[\boxed{0.25}\]

questions.question: \(X\) is a random variable with uniform probability density function in the interval \([-2,10]\). For \(Y = 2X - 6\), the conditional probability \(P(Y \leq 7|X \geq 5)\) (rounded off to three decimal places) is .
questions.explanation:
The random variable \(X\) is uniformly distributed over the interval \([-2,10]\). The probability density function is \[f_X(x) = k, \qquad -2 \leq x \leq 10\] Using the normalization condition, \[\int_{-2}^{10} f_X(x)\,dx = 1\] \[k(10-(-2)) = 1 \Rightarrow\ 12k = 1 \Rightarrow\ k = \frac{1}{12}\] \[\Rightarrow\ f_X(x)=\frac{1}{12}, \qquad -2 \leq x \leq 10\] Given, \(Y = 2X - 6\) We need to evaluate \(P(Y\leq 7 \mid X\geq 5)\) First, simplify the condition on \(Y\): \[2X - 6 \leq 7 \Rightarrow\ 2X \leq 13 \Rightarrow\ X \leq 6.5\] Therefore, using conditional probability, \[P(Y\leq 7 \mid X\geq 5) = P(X\leq 6.5 \mid X\geq 5) = \frac{P(5\leq X\leq 6.5)}{P(X\geq 5)}\] Since the distribution is uniform, \[P(5\leq X\leq 6.5) = \frac{6.5-5}{10-(-2)} = \frac{1.5}{12},\] \[P(X\geq 5) = \frac{10-5}{12} = \frac{5}{12}\] Thus, \[P(Y\leq 7 \mid X\geq 5) = \frac{1.5/12}{5/12} = \frac{1.5}{5} = 0.3\] Rounded to three decimal places, \[0.300\] \[\boxed{0.300}\]
Key points
  • For a uniform distribution over \([a,b]:\), \[f_X(x)=\frac{1}{b-a}\]

questions.question: In the given circuit, the two-port network has the impedance matrix \[\begin{bmatrix} Z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 40 & 60 \\ 60 & 120 \end{bmatrix}\]. The value of \(Z_L\), in \(\Omega\), for which maximum power is transferred to the load is \(\Omega\).
questions.explanation: For Maximum Power Transfer, \(Z_L=Z_{th}\). From the given circuit, we can write the following equations: \[V_{1} = 120 - 10I_{1} \quad \text{--- (1)}\] \[I_{\text{load}} = -I_{2} \quad \text{--- (2)}\] The impedance matrix can be expanded as: \[V_{1} = 40I_{1} + 60I_{2} \quad \text{--- (3)}\] \[V_{2} = 60I_{1} + 120I_{2} \quad \text{--- (4)}\] where \(Z_{th} = \frac{V_{oc}}{I_{sc}}\) looking into the network at Port 2. Now, \(V_{oc} = V_{2}\) when \(I_{2} = 0\). From (4): \[V_{2} = 60I_{1}\] From (3): \[V_{1} = 40I_{1}\] From (1): \[40I_{1} = 120 - 10I_{1}\] \[\Rightarrow 50I_{1} = 120\] \[\Rightarrow I_{1} = \frac{120}{50} = 2.4\,\text{A}\] \[\therefore V_{2} = 60 \times 2.4 = 144\,\text{V}\] Next, \(I_{sc} = -I_{2}\) when \(V_{2} = 0\) (from (2)). questions.question: The output \(y[n]\) of a discrete-time system for an input \(x[n]\) is \[y[n] = \max_{-\infty \le k \le n} |x[k]|.\] The unit impulse response of the system is
questions.explanation:
It is given that \[y(n) = \max_{-\infty \le k \le n} |x(k)|\] We need to obtain its unit impulse response. If the input is a unit impulse, i.e., \(x(k) = \delta(k)\), then the output is the impulse response \(y(n) = h(n)\). So replacing \(x(k)\) by \(\delta(k)\) and \(y(n)\) by \(h(n)\) in the above equation we have: \[h(n) = \max_{-\infty \le k \le n} |\delta(k)|\] Evaluating for \(n = -2\): \[h(-2) = \max_{-\infty \le k \le -2} |\delta(k)|\] \[= \max [|\delta(-\infty)|, \dots, |\delta(-3)|, |\delta(-2)|]\] \[= \max [|0|, |0|, |0|, \dots, |0|] = 0\] From this we can say if \(n \le -1\) then \(h(n) = 0\). If \(n \ge 0\) then \(h(n) = 1\) for all \(n\). For example, evaluating at \(n = 5\): \[h(5) = \max_{-\infty \le k \le 5} |\delta(k)|\] \[= \max [\dots, |\delta(-11)|, |\delta(0)|, |\delta(1)|, |\delta(2)|, |\delta(3)|, |\delta(4)|, |\delta(5)|]\] \[= \max [\dots, |0|, |1|, |0|, |0|, |0|, |0|, |0|] = \max [0, 1, 0, 0, 0] = 1\] Overall: \[h(n) = 0; \quad n < 0\] \[h(n) = 1; \quad n \ge 0\] \[\Rightarrow h(n) = u(n) \text{ i.e., unit step signal}\] Hence the correct answer is option (A). \[\boxed{\text{A) unit step signal u[n].}}\]
Key points
  • The impulse response \(h(n)\) of a system is the output produced when the input is a discrete-time unit impulse \(\delta(n)\).
  • The unit impulse sequence \(\delta(n)\) is defined as \(1\) at \(n=0\) and \(0\) for all \(n \neq 0\).
  • The unit step sequence \(u(n)\) is defined as \(1\) for \(n \ge 0\) and \(0\) for \(n < 0\).

questions.question: \(X(\omega)\) is the Fourier transform of \(x(t)\) shown below. The value of \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |X(\omega)|^2 d\omega\) (rounded off to two decimal places) is _____.
questions.explanation:
We need to obtain the value of \[\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|X(\omega)|^2\,d\omega\] By Parseval's theorem, \[\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|X(\omega)|^2\,d\omega =2\pi\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|x(t)|^2\,dt =2\pi\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}(x(t))^2\,dt\] [Since the given time-domain signal \(x(t)\) is real, the modulus function does not have any role.] We know that shifting does not change the energy of the signal. So, if we define \[y(t)=x(t+1),\] then the energies of \(x(t)\) and \(y(t)\) are the same. Now \(y(t)\) becomes \[\begin{aligned} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|X(\omega)|^2\,d\omega &=2\pi\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}x^2(t)\,dt =2\pi\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}y^2(t)\,dt\\ &=2\times2\pi\int_{0}^{2}y^2(t)\,dt =4\pi\int_{-2}^{0}y^2(t)\,dt \end{aligned}\] Since \(y(t)\) is even, \(y^2(t)\) is also even. \[\begin{aligned} \int_{-a}^{a}y_e(t)\,dt &=2\int_{0}^{a}y_e(t)\,dt =2\int_{-a}^{0}y_e(t)\,dt \end{aligned}\] Therefore, \[\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|X(\omega)|^2\,d\omega =4\pi\left[\int_{-2}^{0}y^2(t)\,dt\right]\] From the shifted waveform, \[\begin{aligned} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|X(\omega)|^2\,d\omega &=4\pi\left[ \int_{-2}^{-1}(t+2)^2\,dt +\int_{-1}^{0}(2t+3)^2\,dt \right]\\ &=4\pi\left[ \int_{-2}^{-1}(t^2+4t+4)\,dt +\int_{-1}^{0}(4t^2+12t+9)\,dt \right]\\ &=4\pi\left[ \left[\frac{t^3}{3}+2t^2+4t\right]_{-2}^{-1} +\left[\frac{4t^3}{3}+6t^2+9t\right]_{-1}^{0} \right]\\ &=4\pi\left[ \frac{1}{3}(-1+8)+2(1-4)+4(-1+2) +\frac{4}{3}(0+1)+6(0-1)+9(0+1) \right]\\ &=4\pi\left[ \frac{2}{3}-6+4+\frac{4}{3}-6+9 \right]\\ &=4\pi\left[\frac{11}{3}+1\right]\\ &=4\pi\left(\frac{14}{3}\right) =\frac{56\pi}{3} =58.64 \end{aligned}\] \[\boxed{58.64}\]
Key points
  • Parseval's theorem gives \(\displaystyle \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|X(\omega)|^2\,d\omega=2\pi\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|x(t)|^2\,dt\).
  • A time shift does not change the energy of a signal.
  • Since the shifted signal \(y(t)\) is even, its squared value \(y^2(t)\) is also even, allowing the integration interval to be reduced.

questions.question: Which one of the following pole-zero corresponds to the transfer function of an LTI system characterized by the input-output difference equation given below? \[y[n] = \sum_{k=0}^{3} (-1)^k x[n - k]\]
questions.explanation:
Method 1
Given : \[y[n] = \sum_{k=0}^{3}(-1)^k\delta[n - k]\] To find impulse response, substitution \(x[n] = \delta[n]\) in the given input output relation. \[h[n] = \sum_{k=0}^{3}(-1)^k\delta[n - k]\] \[h[n] = \delta[n] - \delta[n - 1] + \delta[n - 2] - \delta[n - 3]\] Taking \(z\)-transform both sides to find the transfer function of the system, \[H(z) = 1 - z^{-1} + z^{-2} - z^{-3}\] \[H(z) = \frac{z^3 - z^2 + z - 1}{z^3}\] \[\left. H(z) \right|_{z=+1} = \frac{1 - 1 + 1 - 1}{1} = 0\] So, the system function has a zero at \(z = +1\) that indicates that the low frequency gain of filter is zero. So it will be a high pass filter. To check, finding \(H(z)\) at \(\omega = \pi\) or \(z = -1\) \[\left. H(z) \right|_{z=-1} = \frac{-1 - 1 - 1 - 1}{-1} = 4\] So the system behaves as a HPF and it will not have zero at \(z = -1\). The only option satisfying this is option (D). Hence, the correct option is (D).
Method 2
Given : \[y[n] = \sum_{k=0}^{3}(-1)^k x(n - k)\] \[y(n) = x(n) - x(n - 1) + x(n - 2) - x(n - 3)\] Taking \(z\)-transform on both sides, \[Y(z) = (1 - z^{-1} + z^{-2} - z^{-3})X(z)\] \[\frac{Y(z)}{X(z)} = 1 - z^{-1} + z^{-2} - z^{-3}\] \[H(z) = 1 - z^{-1} + z^{-2} - z^{-3} = \frac{z^3 - z^2 + z - 1}{z^3}\] \(H(z)\) has a pole of order \(3\) at \(z = 0\). To find zero's, equate numerator to zero. \[z^3 - z^2 + z - 1 = 0\] \[(z - 1)(z^2 + 1) = 0\] \[z = 1 \text{ and } z = \pm j\] \(\therefore \quad H(z)\) has zero's at \(z = 1\) and \(z = \pm j\) Hence, the correct option is (D).
\[\boxed{\text{ D }}\]
Key points
  • The transfer function \(H(z)\) is defined as the ratio of the \(z\)-transform of the output to the \(z\)-transform of the input, i.e., \(H(z) = \frac{Y(z)}{X(z)}\).
  • The zeros of a system are the roots of the numerator polynomial of \(H(z)\). Finding a zero at \(z = 1\) (which maps to \(\omega = 0\) on the unit circle) indicates the system attenuates or blocks DC (low-frequency) components.
  • The poles of the system are determined by the roots of the denominator polynomial. A term \(z^3\) in the denominator implies a pole of order 3 at the origin (\(z=0\)).

questions.question: The transfer function of a stable discrete-time LTI sys tem is \(H(z) = \frac{K(z-\alpha)}{z+0.5}\), where \(K\) and \(\alpha\) are real num bers. The value of \(\alpha\) (rounded off to one decimal place) with \(|\alpha| > 1\), for which the magnitude response of the system is constant over all frequencies, is ______.
questions.explanation:
System is all-pass filter. For digital all-pass filter, condition is \[\text{zero} = \frac{1}{\text{pole}^*} \quad \dots(i)\] By given transfer function, \[\text{zero} = \alpha\] \[\text{Pole} = -0.5\] using condition(i), \[\alpha = \frac{1}{-0.5} = -2\] \[\boxed{-2}\]
Key points
  • A system with a constant magnitude response over all frequencies (\(|H(e^{j\omega})| = \text{constant}\)) is an all-pass filter.
  • For a real-valued digital all-pass filter, the poles and zeros occur in reciprocal conjugate pairs. If there is a pole at \(z = p\), there must be a zero at \(z = \frac{1}{p^*}\).
  • Since the coefficients are real in this system, the complex conjugate is just the real value itself, leading to \(\text{zero} = \frac{1}{\text{pole}}\).

questions.subject: signals-and-systems
questions.question: A finite duration discrete-time signal \(x[n]\) is obtained by sampling a continuous - time signal \(x(t) = \cos(200\pi t)\) at sampling instants \(t = \frac{n}{400}, n = 0, 1, \dots, 7\). The 8-point discrete Fourier transform (DFT) is defined a \(X[k] = \sum_{n=0}^{7} x[n]e^{-j\pi nk/4}\) for \(k = 0, 1, \dots, 7\) Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.explanation:
The given continuous-time signal is: \[x(t) = \cos(200\pi t)\] The signal is sampled at instances \(t = \frac{n}{400}\). Thus, the sampling interval is \(T_s = \frac{1}{400}\,\text{s}\). Substituting \(t\) to find the discrete-time sequence \(x[n]\): \[x[n] = x(nT_s) = \cos\left(200\pi \cdot \frac{n}{400}\right) = \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} n\right)\] Using Euler's identity, we can expand the discrete-time sequence: \[x[n] = \frac{1}{2} e^{j\frac{\pi}{2}n} + \frac{1}{2} e^{-j\frac{\pi}{2}n}\] For an \(N\)-point DFT, the standard complex exponential basis sequences are of the form \(e^{j\frac{2\pi k}{N}n}\). Given \(N = 8\), the basis is \(e^{j\frac{\pi}{4}kn}\). We equate the frequencies of our signal's exponential terms to the DFT basis frequencies to determine the non-zero bins (\(k\)): For the positive frequency component: \[\frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4} k \implies k = 2\] For the negative frequency component (which wraps around in a periodic DFT spectrum as \(N - k\)): \[k_2 = N - k = 8 - 2 = 6\] Alternatively, by equating the negative phase directly to the basis phase (with \(2\pi\) periodicity): \[-\frac{\pi}{2} \equiv 2\pi - \frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{3\pi}{2}\] \[\frac{3\pi}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4} k \implies k = 6\] Therefore, only the bins at \(k = 2\) and \(k = 6\) contain energy, meaning only \(X[2]\) and \(X[6]\) (represented as \(X(2)\) and \(X(6)\) in the options) are non-zero. \[\boxed{\text{D) Only $X(2)$ and $X(6)$ are non-zero. }}\]
Key points
  • The discrete frequency corresponding to the \(k\)-th bin in an \(N\)-point DFT is \(\omega_k = \frac{2\pi k}{N}\).
  • A purely real sinusoidal sequence \(x[n] = \cos(\frac{2\pi m n}{N})\) has exactly two non-zero DFT coefficients located at index \(k = m\) and its mirrored position \(k = N - m\).

questions.subject: electronic-devices-circuits
questions.question: A single crystal intrinsic semiconductor is at a temperature of \(300\) K with effective density of states for holes twice that of electrons. The thermal voltage is \(26\) mV. The intrinsic Fermi level is shifted from mid-bandgap energy level by
questions.explanation:
To find the position of the intrinsic Fermi level (\(E_{Fi}\)) relative to the mid-gap energy, we use the standard semiconductor physics relation: \[\frac{E_{C} + E_{V}}{2} - E_{Fi} = \frac{kT}{2} \ln \left( \frac{N_{C}}{N_{V}} \right)\] Given the condition that the effective density of states of electrons is half that of holes: \[N_{C} = \frac{N_{V}}{2} \implies \frac{N_{C}}{N_{V}} = 0.5\] Assuming room temperature (\(T = 300\,\text{K}\)), the thermal voltage \(kT\) is approximately \(0.026\,\text{eV}\). Substituting the values into the equation: \[\frac{E_{C} + E_{V}}{2} - E_{Fi} = \frac{0.026}{2} \ln(0.5) = 0.013 \times (-0.693) \approx -0.00901\,\text{eV} = -9.01\,\text{meV}\] Since magnitude of shift is asked for, answer is \(9.01{meV}\) . \[\boxed{(D) \text{ } 9.01 \text{ meV}}\]
Key points
  • The intrinsic Fermi level \(E_{Fi}\) is located exactly at the mid-gap only if \(N_{C} = N_{V}\).
  • Mid-gap energy is defined as \(E_{midgap} = \frac{E_{C} + E_{V}}{2}\).
  • If \(N_{V} > N_{C}\), the intrinsic Fermi level shifts downward from the mid-gap toward the valence band.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Ensure the sign is correct; \(\ln(0.5)\) is negative, indicating \(E_{Fi}\) is above the mid-gap in this specific mathematical arrangement (\(\text{Midgap} - E_{Fi}\)).
  • Do not confuse \(kT\) (energy in \(\text{eV}\)) with \(kT/q\) (thermal voltage in \(\text{V}\)), although they share the numerical value \(0.0259\) at \(300{K}\).

questions.subject: electronic-devices-circuits
questions.question: Consider the recombination process via bulk traps in a forward biased \(pn\) homojunction diode. The maximum recombination rate is \(U_{max}\). If the electron and the hole capture cross-section are equal, which one of the following is False?
options: With all other parameters unchanged, \(U_{max}\) decreases if the intrinsic carrier density is reduced.
\(U_{max}\) occurs at the edges of the depletion region in the device.
\(U_{max}\) depends exponentially on the applied bias.
With all other parameters unchanged, \(U_{max}\) increases if the thermal velocity of the carriers increases.
questions.explanation:
In a forward-biased \(p\)-\(n\) junction, recombination occurs within the depletion region to return carrier concentrations to their equilibrium values. The recombination rate \(U_{max}\) is influenced by the carrier concentrations which depend exponentially on the applied forward bias \(V_{a}\). At equilibrium, the product of carrier concentrations is \(n_{i}^{2}\). Under forward bias, this becomes: \[n p = n_{i}^{2} e^{V_{a}/V_{T}}\] Since \(V_{a} > 0\), the carrier product exceeds \(n_{i}^{2}\), leading to a recombination current \(I_{recomb}\). Recombination occurs to bring carrier concentration to equilibrium state. Regarding the statements provided in the analysis:
  • As \(n_{i}\) increases, \(n p\) increases, thereby increasing the recombination current \(I_{recomb}\). Thus if \(n_{i}\) increases, \(U_{max}\) decreases. \(\therefore A\) is TRUE.
  • Statement \(B\) suggests that maximum recombination occurs at the edge of the depletion region; however, the highest electric field and the highest recombination rate \(U_{max}\) actually occur at the metallurgical junction (\(x = 0\)). \(\therefore B\) is FALSE.
  • The recombination current \(I_{recomb}\) depends exponentially on the applied voltage \(V_{a}\). \(\therefore C\) is TRUE.
  • If temperature \(T\) increases, the thermal velocity and \(n_{i}\) both increase, which leads to an increase in the recombination current \(I_{recomb}\) and thus recombination rate \(U_{max}\). \(\therefore D\) is TRUE.
\[\boxed{(B)\, U_{max} \text{ occurs at the edges of the depletion region in the device.}}\]
Key points
  • Bulk traps or trap energy levels within the bandgap facilitate the recombination or generation of carriers.
  • Recombination current in the depletion region typically follows an \(e^{V_{a}/\eta V_{T}}\) dependency, where \(\eta\) is the ideality factor (often \(\approx 2\) for recombination).
  • The recombination rate \(R\) is generally highest where the carrier concentrations and trap distributions are most favorable, typically near the junction center.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not assume the recombination rate is uniform throughout the depletion region; it varies with the local electric field and carrier profiles.

questions.subject: electronic-devices-circuits
questions.question: A one-sided abrupt \(pn\) junction diode has a depletion capacitance \(C_D\) of \(50\ pF\) at a reverse bias of \(0.2\ V\). The plot of \(1/C_D^2\) versus the applied voltage \(V\) for this diode is a straight line as shown in the figure below. The slope of the plot is _______ \(\times 10^{20}\ F^{-2}\ V^{-1}\). [figure unavailable]
questions.note: Marks awarded to all (official key: MTA)
questions.explanation:
The depletion (transition) capacitance \(C_{D}\) for a \(p\)-\(n\) junction is given by: \[C_{D} = \frac{A\epsilon}{W}\] For a one-sided \(p^{+}\)-\(n\) junction, the depletion width \(W\) is expressed as: \[W = \sqrt{\frac{2\epsilon (V_{bi} - V)}{eN_{D}}}\] where \(V\) is the applied potential from anode to cathode. Substituting \(W\) into the capacitance formula: \[C_{D} = \frac{A\epsilon}{\sqrt{\frac{2\epsilon (V_{bi} - V)}{eN_{D}}}} \implies \frac{1}{C_{D}^{2}} = \frac{2}{A^{2}\epsilon eN_{D}}(V_{bi} - V)\] [figure unavailable] From the provided graph of \(y = \frac{1}{C_{D}^{2}}\) versus \(x = V\):
  • The value of \(\frac{1}{C_{D}^{2}}\) becomes zero at the \(x\)-intercept, which corresponds to \(V = V_{bi}\).
  • At \(x_{1} = V_{bi}\), \(y_{1} = 0\).
  • At \(x_{2} = -0.2\,\text{V}\), the value is \(y_{2} = \frac{1}{(50 \times 10^{-12})^{2}} = 4 \times 10^{20}\,\text{F}^{-2}\).
The slope of the line is calculated as: \[\text{Slope} = \frac{y_{2} - y_{1}}{x_{2} - x_{1}} = \frac{4 \times 10^{20} - 0}{-0.2 - V_{bi}}\] Since the built-in potential \(V_{bi}\) is not explicitly provided in the problem statement, the slope and subsequent parameters cannot be uniquely determined. As per the GATE official answer key, this question was awarded Marks to All (MTA).
Key points
  • Depletion Capacitance: \(C_{D}\) is inversely proportional to the square root of the reverse bias voltage.
  • C-V Characterization: A plot of \(1/C_{D}^{2}\) vs. \(V\) yields a straight line where the \(x\)-intercept represents the built-in potential \(V_{bi}\).
  • Doping Determination: The slope of the \(1/C_{D}^{2}\) plot is inversely proportional to the doping concentration \(N_{D}\).
Mistakes to avoid
  • Ensure the applied voltage \(V\) is treated correctly; for reverse bias, \(V\) is negative, making \((V_{bi} - V)\) positive.
  • Do not confuse depletion capacitance (dominant in reverse bias) with diffusion capacitance (dominant in forward bias).

questions.subject: electronic-devices-circuits
questions.question: The band diagram of a p-type semiconductor with a band-gap of \(1\text{ eV}\) is shown. Using this semiconductor, a MOS capacitor having \(V_{TH}\) of \(-0.16\text{ V}\), \(C'_{ox}\) of \(100\text{ nF/cm}^2\) and a metal work function of \(3.87\text{ eV}\) is fabricated. There is no charge within the oxide. If the voltage across the capacitor is \(V_{TH}\), the magnitude of depletion charge per unit area (in \(\text{C/cm}^2\)) is [figure unavailable]
questions.explanation:
For a MOS capacitor, the threshold voltage is given by: \[V_T = \phi_{ms} - \frac{Q_{ox}}{C_{ox}} + \frac{Q'_d}{C_{ox}} + 2\phi_{F_p}\] The given parameters are: \[\phi_m = 3.87, \quad \phi_s = 4.8\] \[\text {Thus, } \phi_{ms} = \phi_m - \phi_s =-0.93\] Computing \(\phi_{F_p}\): \[\phi_{F_p} = E_i - E_F = 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.3\,\text{V}\] Substituting into the threshold voltage equation with \(V_T = -0.16\,\text{V}\) and \(Q_{ox} = 0\): \[-0.16 = -0.93 - 0 + \frac{Q'_d}{C_{ox}} + 2 \times 0.3\] Solving for \(\dfrac{Q'_d}{C_{ox}}\): \[-\frac{Q'_d}{C_{ox}} = 0.6 + 0.16 - 0.93 = -0.17\,\text{V}\] Therefore, the depletion charge: \[Q_d = 0.17 \times C_{ox} = 0.17 \times 100 \times 10^{-9} = 1.7 \times 10^{-8}\,\text{C/cm}^2\] \[\boxed{(A)\,1.7 \times 10^{-8}}\]
Key points
  • \(\phi_s\) is the semiconductor work function, and is given by the difference in energy between Vacuum Level and semiconductor Fermi level.
  • The depletion charge \(Q_d\) is inherently negative for a p-type MOS structure (ionized acceptors carry negative charge).

questions.subject: electronic-devices-circuits
questions.question: A pn junction solar cell of area \(1.0 \, cm^2\), illuminated uniformly with \(100\, mW cm^{-2}\), has the following parameters: Efficiency = \(15\%\), open circuit voltage = \(0.7 V\), fill factor = \(0.8\), and thickness = \(200 \mu m\). The charge of an electron is \(1.6 \times 10^{-19} C\). The average optical generation rate (in \(cm^{-3}s^{-1}\)) is
questions.explanation:
Efficiency of solar cell is given by: \[\eta=\frac{(FF) V_{OC} I_{SC}}{P_{in}}\] Substituting given values: \[0.15 = \frac{0.8 \times 0.7 \times I_{SC}}{100 mW}\] \[I_{SC} = \frac{15}{0.56} mA\] Optical generation Rate is given by: \[G_L = \frac{I_{SC}}{q\times \text{Area} \times \text{Thickness}}\] \[G_L = \frac{15 \times 10^{-3}}{0.56 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 1 \times 200 \times 10^{-4}}\] \[G_L = 0.837 \times10^{19} \approx 0.84\times10^{19}\] \[\boxed{(A)\, 0.84\times10^{19}}\]
Key points
  • Solar cell efficiency is \(\eta = (FF \times V_{OC} \times I_{SC})/P_{in}\); rearranging gives \(I_{SC} = \eta P_{in}/(FF \times V_{OC})\).
  • The optical generation rate \(G_L = I_{SC}/(q \times \text{Area} \times \text{Thickness})\); it represents the number of electron-hole pairs generated per unit volume per second.
  • Fill Factor \(FF = P_{\max}/(V_{OC} \times I_{SC})\); a higher \(FF\) (closer to 1) indicates a more ideal solar cell.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not confuse \(I_{SC}\) (short-circuit current) with \(I_0\) (reverse saturation current); they are fundamentally different -- \(I_{SC}\) is the photogenerated current while \(I_0\) is the dark diode leakage current.

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: In the circuit shown below, all the components are ideal and the input voltage is sinusoidal. The magnitude of the steady-state output \(V_o\) (rounded off to two decimal places) is V.
questions.explanation:
Method 1
The first half of the circuit is a positive clamper circuit which clamps the input voltage above zero.
Given rms value of sinusoidal input \[\frac{V_m}{\sqrt{2}} = 230 \Rightarrow V_m = \sqrt{2} \times 230\] Second half of the circuit is a peak detector will detect the maximum value \(= 2V_m = 2 \times 230(\sqrt{2}) = 650.53\) \[\boxed{\text{Hence the steady state output } V_0 = 650.53\text{V}}\]
Method 2
The given circuit is a voltage doubler. \[V_0 = 2V_m = 2 \times 230\sqrt{2} = 650.54\,\text{V}\] \[\boxed{\text{Hence the steady state output } V_0 = 650.54\text{V}}\]
Key points
  • A full-wave voltage doubler (or a cascade of a clamper and a peak detector) produces a steady-state output DC voltage equal to twice the peak value of the input sinusoidal signal.
  • The peak value \(V_m\) is derived from the RMS voltage using the relation \(V_m = V_{\text{rms}} \times \sqrt{2}\).

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: Using the incremental low frequency small-signal model of the MOS device, the Norton equivalent resistance of the following circuit is
questions.explanation:
The small signal equivalent circuit is shown below, Applying KVL in loop 1, \[-V_{gs} - V_x = 0\] \[V_{gs} = -V_x \quad \dots \text{(i)}\] Applying KVL in loop 2, \[V_x - r_{ds}(I_x + g_m V_{gs}) - R I_x = 0\] From equation (i), putting \(V_{gs} = -V_x\), \[+V_x - r_{ds}I_x + g_m V_x r_{ds} - R I_x = 0\] \[V_x(1 + g_m r_{ds}) = I_x(r_{ds} + R)\] \[\frac{V_x}{I_x} = R_N = \frac{r_{ds} + R}{1 + g_m r_{ds}}\] \[\boxed{\text{(B)}\quad \dfrac{r_{ds}+R}{1+g_mr_{ds}}}\]
Key points
  • To calculate the Norton equivalent resistance (\(R_N\)) looking into a specific terminal, apply a test voltage source \(V_x\) at that terminal and evaluate the current \(I_x\) supplied by the source. The resistance is \(R_N = \frac{V_x}{I_x}\).
  • For a common-gate topology (looking into the source), the input resistance is not simply \(\frac{1}{g_m}\) when \(r_{ds}\) is finite and a drain resistor \(R\) is present. The general expression becomes \(R_{in} = \frac{r_{ds} + R}{1 + g_m r_{ds}}\).

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: An enhancement MOSFET of threshold voltage \(3 \text{ V}\) is being used in the sample and hold circuit given below. Assume that the substrate of the MOS device is connected to \(-10 \text{ V}\). If the input voltage \(V_I\) lies between \(\pm 10 \text{ V}\), the minimum and the maximum values of \(V_G\) required for proper sampling and holding respectively, are
questions.explanation:
Sample and hold circuit is an analog device that samples the voltage of a continuously varying signal and holds its signal value at a constant level for a specified period. For proper sampling operation, the MOSFET should be on so that the capacitor can charge upto the input voltage i.e. \[V_{GS} > V_T\] For proper holding operation, the MOSFET should be off so that the capacitor can hold its charge i.e. \[V_{GS} < V_T\] Given: \(V_T = 3\,\text{V}\), \(V_{(I)\min} = -10\,\text{V}\), \(V_{(I)\max} = 10\,\text{V}\) The MOSFET should be on for sampling operation, i.e. \[V_{GS} > V_T\] \[V_G - V_{(I)\max} > V_T\] \[V_G - 10 > 3\] \[V_G > 13\,\text{V}\] The MOSFET should be off for holding operation, i.e. \[V_{GS} < V_T\] \[V_G - V_{(I)\min} < V_T\] \[V_G - (-10) < 3\] \[V_G < -7\,\text{V}\] Hence, the minimum and the maximum values of \(V_G\) required for proper sampling and holding respectively, are \(13\,\text{V}\) and \(-7\,\text{V}\) respectively. \[\boxed{\text{(C)}\quad 13\,\text{V}\ \text{and}\ -7\,\text{V}}\]
Key points
  • During sampling phase, MOSFET must be fully turned ON, satisfying the condition \(V_{GS} > V_T\) even for the most positive possible input voltage level (\(V_{(I)\max}\)).
  • During holding phase, MOSFET must be fully turned OFF, satisfying the condition \(V_{GS} < V_T\) even for the most negative possible input voltage level (\(V_{(I)\min}\)).

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: The components in the circuit shown below are ideal. If the op-amp is in positive feedback and the input voltage \(V_i\) is a sine wave of amplitude \(1\text{ V}\), the output voltage \(V_o\) is
options: a non-inverted sine wave of \(2\text{ V}\) amplitude.
an inverted sine wave of \(1\text{ V}\) amplitude.
a square wave of \(5\text{ V}\) amplitude.
a constant of either \(+5\text{ V}\) or \(-5\text{ V}\).
questions.explanation:
Given circuit is a non-inverting Schmitt trigger From given figure, \(V_y = 0\) \[V_{x} = \frac{V_i \times 1 + V_o \times 1}{1 + 1}\] \[V_{x} = \frac{V_i + V_o}{2}\] If \(V_{x} > V_y\) then \(V_o = +V_{sat}\) and If \(V_{x} < V_y\) then \(V_o = -V_{sat}\) Assume \(V_o = +5\,\text{V}\), then \[\frac{V_i + V_o}{2} > 0\] \[\frac{V_i + 5}{2} > 0\] \[V_i > -5\] so, if \(V_i>-5\) then \(V_0\) switches from -5 V to +5 V. Assume \(V_0=-5 \text{ V}\), then \[\frac{V_i + V_o}{2}< 0\] \[\frac{V_i - 5}{2} < 0\] \[V_i < 5\] So, if \(V_i<5\) then \(V_0\) will switch from +5 V to -5 V. Here, input voltage \(V_i\) is not crossing either lower and upper threshold voltage so output will not change and remain in its initial state of either \(+5\,\text{V}\) or \(-5\,\text{V}\) depending on how input arrived initially. Therefore, output of given Schmitt trigger is constant of either \(+5\,\text{V}\) or \(-5\,\text{V}\) \[\boxed{\text{(D)\quad constant of either } +5\,\text{V} \text{ or } -5\,\text{V}}\]
Key points
  • In a schmitt trigger, the transition of output states requires the input voltage to exceed the upper threshold point (\(V_{UTP}\)) or drop below the lower threshold point (\(V_{LTP}\)).
  • If the input signal's peak amplitude (\(1\,\text{V}\)) is smaller than the magnitude of the threshold voltages (\(\pm 5\,\text{V}\)), the op-amp will not toggle and remains saturated at its initial state (either \(+5\,\text{V}\) or \(-5\,\text{V}\)).

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: In the circuit shown below, all the components are ideal. If \(V_i\) is \(+2\text{ V}\), the current \(I_o\) sourced by the op-amp is ________ mA.
questions.explanation: Given Op-Amp circuit is shown in below figure, Since this is a -ve feedback Op-Amp circuit. So we can apply virtual grounded concept. So, \(V_x = V_i = 2\,\text{V}\). Applying KCL at node \(V_x\), \[\frac{V_x - 0}{1\,\text{k}} + \frac{V_x - V_o}{1\,\text{k}} + 0 = 0\] \[\frac{2 - 0}{1\,\text{k}} + \frac{2 - V_o}{1\,\text{k}} = 0\] \[V_o = 4\,\text{V}\] Applying KCL at node \(V_o\), \[\frac{V_o - V_x}{1\,\text{k}} + \frac{V_o - 0}{1\,\text{k}} - I_o = 0\] \[\frac{4 - 2}{1\,\text{k}} + \frac{4}{1\,\text{k}} = I_o\] \[I_o = 6\,\text{mA}\] \[\boxed{I_0=6\text{ mA}}\]

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: The components in the circuit given below are ideal. If \(R = 2\,\text{k}\Omega\) and \(C = 1\,\mu\text{F}\), the \(-3\text{ dB}\) cut-off frequency of the circuit in Hz is
questions.explanation:
Given circuit is shown in below figure, This is an inverting integrator circuit. From virtual ground concept, \[V_I = V_{N_I} = 0\] Applying KCL at \(V_I\), \[\frac{V_I - 0}{2R} + \frac{V_I - 0}{\frac{1}{2sC}} + \frac{V_I - V_i}{R} + \frac{V_I - V_0}{\frac{1}{sC}} + \frac{V_I - V_0}{R} = 0\] Putting \(V_I = 0\), \[\frac{0 - V_i}{R} + \frac{0 - V_0}{\frac{1}{sC}} + \frac{0 - V_0}{R} = 0\] \[\frac{-V_i}{R} = \frac{V_0(1 + sRC)}{R}\] \[V_0 = \frac{-V_i}{(1 + sRC)}\] \[\frac{V_0}{V_i} = H(s) = \frac{-1}{1 + sRC}\] Pole at \(s = \frac{-1}{RC}\), so \[\omega_H = \frac{1}{RC}\] \[f_H = \frac{1}{2\pi RC} = \frac{1}{2\pi \times 2 \times 10^3 \times 10^{-6}}\] \[f_H = 79.58\,\text{Hz}\] \[\boxed{\text{(D)\quad}79.58}\]
Key points
  • Cut-off Frequency: For a single-pole system with the transfer function \(H(s) = \frac{A}{1 + sRC}\), the \(-3\text{ dB}\) cut-off frequency is determined by the pole location, which gives \(f_H = \frac{1}{2\pi RC}\).

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: In the voltage regulator shown below, \(V_I\) is the unregulated input at \(15\text{ V}\). Assume \(V_{BE} = 0.7\text{ V}\) and the base current is negligible for both the BJTs. If the regulated output \(V_O\) is \(9\text{ V}\), the value of \(R_2\) is \(\Omega\).
questions.explanation:
Given circuit is, Since the base current of both the transistors is negligible, the current through \(R_1\) will pass straight to \(R_2\). Therefore \(R_1, R_2\) will be in series. Using voltage divider rule, we can write: \[\frac{V_O \times R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = V_{x} \quad \dots (1)\] Applying KVL from \(V_{x}\) to Zener to ground, we can write: \[V_{x} - V_{BE} - 3.3 = 0\] Given: \[V_{BE} = 0.7\] \[V_{x} = 3.3 + 0.7 = 4\,\text{V}\] Putting this in equation (1), we get: \[\frac{V_O \times R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = 4\] \[\frac{9 \times R_2}{1000 + R_2} = 4\] \[9R_2 = 4(1000 + R_2)\] \[9R_2 = 4000 + 4R_2\] \[5 \times R_2 = 4000\] \[\boxed{R_2 = 800\,\Omega}\]
Key points
  • When the base current is negligible, the feedback resistors (\(R_1\) and \(R_2\)) form an unloaded voltage divider.
  • By applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) in the bottom loop, we can get the voltage at the feedback node.

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: For the BJT in the amplifier shown below, \(V_{BE} = 0.7\text{ V}\), \(kT/q = 26\text{ mV}\). Assume that BJT output resistance (\(r_o\)) is very high and the base current is negligible. The capacitors are also assumed to be short circuited at signal frequencies. The input \(v_i\) is direct coupled. The low frequency voltage gain \(v_o/v_i\) of the amplifier is
questions.explanation:
DC Analysis : For DC analysis all the capacitors are open-circuited as shown below. Given that the base current is negligible, so we can write: \[I_C \approx I_E\] Applying KVL for the base-emitter loop, we get: \[0 - V_{BE} - I_C(20\,\text{k}\Omega) + 10 = 0\] \[I_C = \frac{10 - 0.7}{20\,\text{k}\Omega}\] \[I_C = 0.465\,\text{mA}\] \[g_m = \frac{I_C}{V_T} = \frac{0.465\,\text{mA}}{26\,\text{mV}}\] \[g_m = 0.01788\,\text{A/V}\] AC analysis: Given that for AC analysis, capacitors are shorted and \(r_0\) is very high. Hence the The small signal model is drawn as: Here \(V_i = V_\pi\). Applying KVL in output loop, \[V_0 = -g_mV_\pi(R_C ||R_L)\] The small-signal gain will be: \[A_v = -g_m (R_C \parallel R_L)\] \[A_v = -(0.01788) (10\,\text{k}\Omega \parallel 10\,\text{k}\Omega)\] \[A_v = -0.01788 \times 5\,\text{k}\Omega\] \[A_v = -89.42\] \[\boxed{\text{(A)\quad -89.42}}\]
Key points
  • DC Analysis: During DC analysis, capacitors act as open circuits.
  • Transconductance (\(g_m\)): It is a key small-signal parameter defined as \(g_m = \frac{I_C}{V_T}\), where \(V_T = \frac{kT}{q}\) is the thermal voltage.
  • AC Analysis: For small-signal AC analysis, coupling and bypass capacitors act as short circuits, and DC voltage sources are grounded.

questions.question: \(P\), \(Q\), and \(R\) are the decimal integers corresponding to the 4-bit binary number \(1100\) considered in signed magnitude, \(1\)'s complement, and \(2\)'s complement representations, respectively. The 6-bit \(2\)'s complement representation of \((P + Q + R)\) is
questions.explanation:
Given: \(4\)-bit binary number \((1100)_2\). Since \(\text{MSB} = 1\), it represents a negative number in all three systems.
  • Signed Magnitude (\(P\)):
    \(\text{MSB} = 1\) (negative), remaining bits \(100 = 4\). \[P = -4\]
  • 1's Complement (\(Q\)):
    Keep \(\text{MSB} = 1\). Take 1's complement of magnitude bits: \(100 \rightarrow 011 = 3\). \[Q = -3\]
  • 2's Complement (\(R\)):
    Keep \(\text{MSB} = 1\). Take 2's complement of magnitude bits: \(100 \rightarrow 011 + 1 = 100 = 4\). \[R = -4\]
Sum of the decimal integers: \[P + Q + R = -4 + (-3) + (-4) = -11\] To represent \(-11\) in \(6\)-bit \(2\)'s complement form: \[+11 = 001011\] \[\text{1's complement of } +11 = 110100\] \[\text{2's complement of } +11 = 110100 + 1 = 110101\] Hence, the correct option is (A). \[\boxed{\text{(A) }110101}\]
Key points
  • In signed number systems, \(\text{MSB} = 0\) indicates a positive number, and \(\text{MSB} = 1\) indicates a negative number.
  • To find the magnitude of a negative number in complement systems, complement the magnitude bits while keeping the sign bit intact.

questions.question: For the components in the sequential circuit shown below, \(t_{pd}\) is the propagation delay, \(t_{setup}\) is the setup time, and \(t_{hold}\) is the hold time. The maximum clock frequency (rounded off to the nearest integer), at which the given circuit can operate reliably, is MHz.
questions.explanation:
For a standard sequential circuit as given above the formula for the minimum clock period (\(T_{clk}\)) to avoid setup time violations is: \[\boxed{T_{clk} \geq t_{pd1} + T_{comb} + t_{su2}}\] (refer video for derivation) Let us evaluate the two distinct data path loops in the circuit: Path 1: From \(\text{FF}_1\) to \(\text{FF}_2\)
  • Launching flip-flop: \(\text{FF}_1 \implies t_{\text{pd1}} = 3\,\text{ns}\)
  • Combinational delay (\(\text{XOR} + \text{NAND}\)): \(t_{\text{pd(combinational1)}} = 2\,\text{ns} + 2\,\text{ns} = 4\,\text{ns}\)
  • Capturing flip-flop: \(\text{FF}_2 \implies t_{\text{setup2}} = 4\,\text{ns}\)
\[T_{\text{min1}} = 3\,\text{ns} + 4\,\text{ns} + 4\,\text{ns} = 11\,\text{ns}\] Path 2: From \(\text{FF}_2\) to \(\text{FF}_1\)
  • Launching flip-flop: \(\text{FF}_2 \implies t_{\text{pd2}} = 8\,\text{ns}\)
  • Combinational delay: Direct feedback connection \(\implies t_{\text{pd(combinational2)}} = 0\,\text{ns}\)
  • Capturing flip-flop: \(\text{FF}_1 \implies t_{\text{setup1}} = 5\,\text{ns}\)
\[T_{\text{min2}} = 8\,\text{ns} + 0\,\text{ns} + 5\,\text{ns} = 13\,\text{ns}\] Maximum Clock Frequency
The minimum allowable clock period \(T_{\text{clk}}\) must safely satisfy both setup constraints: \[T_{\text{clk}} = \max(T_{\text{min1}},\, T_{\text{min2}}) = \max(11\,\text{ns},\, 13\,\text{ns}) = 13\,\text{ns}\] The maximum reliable operating clock frequency \(f_{\text{max}}\) is: \[f_{\text{max}} = \frac{1}{T_{\text{clk}}} = \frac{1}{13\,\text{ns}} \approx 76.92\,\text{MHz}\] Rounding off to the nearest integer: \[f_{\text{max}} \approx 77\,\text{MHz}\] \[\boxed{77}\]
Key points
  • Minimum clock period is bounded by the longest path constraint: \(T_{\text{clk}} = \max(T_{\text{paths}})\).
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not blindly add the combinational delays to every loop; analyze the exact connectivity shown in the schematic.
  • Ensure setup time is always taken from the receiving (\(\text{FF}_{\text{capture}}\)) flip-flop.

questions.subject: digital-electronics
questions.question: A 10-bit D/A converter is calibrated over the full range from \(0\) to \(10\)~V. If the input to the D/A converter is \(13\text{A}\) (in hex), the output (rounded off to three decimal places) is V.
questions.explanation:
Given data from the problem statement:
  • Number of bits: \(n = 10\)
  • Full-scale voltage range: \(V_{\text{FSR}} = 10\,\text{V}\)
  • Hexadecimal digital input: \((13\text{A})_{16}\)
Converting the hexadecimal input to its decimal equivalent: \[(13\text{A})_{16} = 1 \times 16^2 + 3 \times 16^1 + 10 \times 16^0 = 256 + 48 + 10 = (314)_{10}\] The step size (resolution) of the \(10\)-bit D/A converter is computed as: \[\text{Resolution } (R) = \frac{V_{\text{FSR}}}{2^n - 1} = \frac{10\,\text{V}}{2^{10} - 1} = \frac{10}{1023} \approx 9.77517 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{V}\] The analog output voltage \(V_o\) is given by: \[V_o = \text{Resolution } (R) \times \text{Decimal Equivalent}\] \[V_o = \left(\frac{10}{1023}\right) \times 314 = \frac{3140}{1023} \approx 3.0694\,\text{V}\] Rounding off to three decimal places yields the final analog output voltage as \(3.069\,\text{V}\). \[\boxed{3.069}\]
Key points
  • The step size or resolution of an \(n\)-bit DAC over a full-scale range is given by \(R = \frac{V_{\text{FSR}}}{2^n - 1}\).
  • Hexadecimal values must always be completely expanded into base-10 weights before evaluating the final output signal voltage.

questions.question: In an 8085 microprocessor, the number of address lines required to access a 16 K byte memory bank is .
questions.explanation:
The memory size to be accessed is given as \(16\text{ K bytes}\). The relationship between memory capacity and the number of address lines (\(n\)) required is: \[\text{Memory Size} = 2^n \text{ bytes}\] Expressing \(16\text{ K}\) as a power of \(2\): \[16\text{ K} = 16 \times 1024 = 2^4 \times 2^{10} = 2^{14}\] Equating the exponents: \[2^n = 2^{14} \implies n = 14\] Thus, the number of address lines required is \(14\). \[\boxed{14}\]
Key points
  • \(1\text{ K}\) (Kilo) in digital memory conversion is equal to \(2^{10} = 1024\).
  • \(n\) address lines can uniquely address \(2^n\) distinct memory locations.

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: Consider the following closed loop control system where \(G(s) = \dfrac{1}{s(s+1)}\) and \(C(s) = K \dfrac{s+1}{s+3}\). If the steady state error for a unit ramp input is \(0.1\), then the value of \(K\) is
questions.explanation:
Open loop transfer function is given by, \[\text{OLTF} = G(s)C(s)\] \[G'(s) = \frac{1}{s(s+1)} \frac{K(s+1)}{(s+3)} = \frac{K}{s(s+3)}\] Given: For ramp input, \(e_{ss} = 0.1\) \(K_v (\text{Velocity error constant}) :\) \[K_v = \lim_{s \to 0} s[\text{OLTF}]\] \[K_v = \lim_{s \to 0} s G'(s) = \lim_{s \to 0} s \frac{K}{s(s+3)} = \frac{K}{3}\] Steady state error is given by, \[e_{ss} = \frac{1}{K_v} \implies e_{ss} = \frac{1}{K/3} = \frac{3}{K}\] So, \(\dfrac{3}{K} = 0.1 \implies K = 30\) \[\boxed{K=30}\]
Key points
Shortcut to find \(K_v\):
\[K_v= \frac{\text{Numerator Constant of OLTF}}{\text{Denominator Constant of OLTF}}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: The loop transfer function of a negative feedback system is \[G(s)H(s) = \frac{K(s + 11)}{s(s + 2)(s + 8)}\] The value of \(K\), for which the system is marginally stable, is
questions.explanation:
Characteristic equation \(q(s)\) for the given open-loop system will be: \[q(s) = s^{3} + 10s^{2} + (16 + K)s + 11K = 0\]
Method 1
R-H Table: \[\begin{array}{c|cc} s^{3} & 1 & 16 + K \\ s^{2} & 10 & 11K \\ s^{1} & \dfrac{10(16 + K) - 11K}{10} & 0 \\ s^{0} & 11K & 0 \end{array}\] For marginal stability, the \(s^{1}\) row must be zero: \[\frac{10(16 + K) - 11K}{10} = 0\] \[160 + 10K - 11K = 0\] \[\boxed{K = 160}\]
Method 2
Shortcut Method : At \(K = K_{\text{marginal}}\), \[\text{Inner product} = \text{Outer product}\] \[1 \times 11K_{\text{marginal}} = 10(16 + K_{\text{marginal}})\] \[11K_{\text{marginal}} - 10K_{\text{marginal}} = 160\] \[\boxed{K_{\text{marginal}} = 160}\]
Key points
This 'Inner Product = Outer Product' shortcut is a direct derivation from the Routh-Hurwitz \(s^1\) row being zero.

questions.question: The characteristic equation of a system is \(s^{3} + 3s^{2} + (K + 2)s + 3K = 0\) In the root locus plot for the given system, as \(K\) varies from \(0\) to \(\infty\), the break-away or break-in point(s) lie within
questions.explanation:
Given: \(\text{C.E} = s^3 + 3s^2 + (2 + K)s + 3K = 0\) Converting to standard form: \(1 + G(s)H(s) = 0\) \[s^3 + 3s^2 + 2s + K(s + 3) = 0\] \[1 + \frac{K(s + 3)}{s^3 + 3s^2 + 2s} = 0\] \[1 + \frac{K(s + 3)}{s(s + 1)(s + 2)} = 0\] Where \(G(s)H(s)\) is the open loop transfer function: \[G(s)H(s) = \frac{K(s + 3)}{s(s + 1)(s + 2)}\] Since there are poles located at \(-1\) and \(0\), the breakaway point will lie in between \(-1\) and \(0\). \[\boxed{(A) \ \ \text{(-1, 0)}}\]
Key points
  • A point on the real axis lies on the root locus if the total number of open-loop poles and zeros to its right is odd.
  • Breakaway points typically occur between two adjacent poles on the real axis if that segment is part of the root locus. Break-in points typically occur between two adjacent zeros on the real axis if that segment is part of the root locus.

questions.ref: Polar Plot & Frequency Response of 2nd Order Systems Q1
questions.question: A system with transfer function \[G(s) = \frac{1}{(s+1)(s+a)}\] where \(a > 0\), is subjected to an input \(5\cos 3t\). The steady state output of the system is \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \cos(3t - 1.892)\). The value of \(a\) is
questions.explanation:
Given, \[G(s)=\frac{1}{(s+1)(s+a)}, \qquad a>0\] Input: \[x(t)=5\cos 3t\] Steady-state output: \[y(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\cos(3t-1.892)\] For a sinusoidal input, the steady-state output is \[y(t)=A|G(j\omega_{0})| \cos\left( \omega_{0}t+\angle G(j\omega_{0}) \right)\] Here, \[\omega_{0}=3\,\text{rad/s}\] Substituting \(s=j\omega\), \[G(j\omega)=\frac{1}{(1+j\omega)(a+j\omega)}\] Magnitude: \[|G(j\omega)| = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+\omega^{2}}\sqrt{a^{2}+\omega^{2}}}\] At \(\omega=3\), \[|G(j3)| = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+3^{2}}\sqrt{a^{2}+3^{2}}}\] \[= \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}\sqrt{a^{2}+9}}\] Output amplitude is \[5\times |G(j3)| = \frac{5}{\sqrt{10}\sqrt{a^{2}+9}}\] Comparing with the given output amplitude, \[\frac{5}{\sqrt{10}\sqrt{a^{2}+9}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\] \[\frac{25}{10(a^{2}+9)} = \frac{1}{10}\] \[25=a^{2}+9\] \[a^{2}=16\] \[a=\pm4\] Since \(a>0\), \[a=4\] \[\boxed{4}\]
Key points
  • For sinusoidal input \(A\cos(\omega_{0}t)\), the steady-state output is obtained using frequency response \(G(j\omega_{0})\).
  • Output amplitude is multiplied by \(|G(j\omega_{0})|\).
  • Output phase shift is \(\angle G(j\omega_{0})\).
  • The input frequency remains unchanged in steady-state response.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not forget to substitute \(\omega_{0}\) equal to the input frequency before calculating magnitude and phase.
  • Do not change the input frequency in the steady-state output expression.
  • Do not take the negative value of \(a\) since \(a>0\) is given.

questions.explanation:
Given, \[\phi(t)= \begin{cases} 1, & 5\le t\le7 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\] \[S_W(f)=3\;\text{Watts/Hz}\] \[R_W(\tau)=3\delta(\tau)=3\delta(t_1-t_2)\] Variance is defined as \[\mathrm{Var}[y]=E[y^2]-E[y]^2\] The output of the correlator is \[y=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} W(t)\phi(t)\,dt\] Since white noise has zero mean, \(E[W(t)]=0\). Therefore, \[E[y] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} E[W(t)]\phi(t)\,dt = 0\] Now, \[E[y^2]=E[y\cdot y]\] \[= E\left[ \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}W(t_1)\phi(t_1)\,dt_1 \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}W(t_2)\phi(t_2)\,dt_2 \right]\] \[= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} E[W(t_1)W(t_2)] \phi(t_1)\phi(t_2) \,dt_1dt_2\] Using \(E[W(t_1)W(t_2)]=R_W(t_1-t_2)\), \[E[y^2] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} R_W(t_1-t_2)\phi(t_1)\phi(t_2) \,dt_1dt_2\] Substituting \(R_W(t_1-t_2)=3\delta(t_1-t_2)\), \[E[y^2] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} 3\delta(t_1-t_2)\phi(t_1)\phi(t_2) \,dt_1dt_2\] Using the sifting property of delta function, \(t_1=t_2=t\). Hence, \[E[y^2] = 3\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\phi^2(t)\,dt\] \[= 3\times \text{Energy}[\phi(t)]\] Now, \(\phi(t)=1\) for \(5\le t\le7\). Therefore, \[\text{Energy}[\phi(t)] = \int_{5}^{7}1^2\,dt = 2\] Thus, \[E[y^2]=3\times2=6\] Also, \(E[y]^2=0\). Therefore, \[\mathrm{Var}[y] = E[y^2]-E[y]^2 = 6-0\] \[\boxed{ \mathrm{Var}[y]=6 }\] Equivalent PSD approach: \[S_Y(f)=|H(f)|^2S_W(f)\] \[\sigma_Y^2 = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}S_Y(f)\,df = \frac{N_0}{2} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|H(f)|^2\,df\] Using Parseval energy theorem, \[\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|H(f)|^2\,df = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|\phi(t)|^2\,dt = E_{\phi}\] Hence, \[\sigma_Y^2 = \left(\frac{N_0}{2}\right)E_{\phi} = 3\times2 = 6\] \[\boxed{ \sigma_Y^2=6 }\]
Key points
  • Output Variance of White Noise: For white noise passed through a correlator or LTI system, \[\sigma_Y^2=\frac{N_0}{2}E_\phi\] where \(E_\phi\) is the energy of the impulse response or basis function.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Confusing Power and Energy: Do not directly substitute signal duration in place of energy; first compute \[E_\phi=\int |\phi(t)|^2dt\]
  • Incorrect Delta Function Handling: While using \[\delta(t_1-t_2)\] ensure the sifting property is applied correctly to reduce the double integral.
  • Missing Zero Mean Property: White Gaussian noise has zero mean, so \[E[Y]^2=0\] should not be ignored in variance calculations.

questions.question: A digital communication system transmits a block of \(N\) bits. The probability of error in decoding a bit is \(\alpha\). The error event of each bit is independent of the error events of the other bits. The received block is declared erroneous if at least one of its bits is decoded wrongly. The probability that the received block is erroneous is
questions.explanation: Theory: Assuming independent bit errors, the probability that all \(N\) bits are received correctly is the product of the individual bit-correct probabilities. Given that the probability of error in decoding a single bit is \[P_e=\alpha,\]the probability of correct decoding of a single bit is \[P_c=1-\alpha.\]For an \(N\)-bit block, the probability that all \(N\) bits are received correctly is \[P(\text{no error in block}) = (1-\alpha)(1-\alpha)\cdots(1-\alpha)\] \[= (1-\alpha)^N.\]Therefore, the probability that the received block contains at least one error is \[P(\text{erroneous block}) = 1-P(\text{no error in block})\] \[= 1-(1-\alpha)^N.\]Hence, \[\boxed{(D) 1-(1-\alpha)^N }\]

questions.question: In a digital communication system, a symbol \(S\) randomly chosen from the set \(\{s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4\}\) is transmitted. It is given that \(s_1=-3\) , \(s_2=-1\) ,\(s_3=+1\), and \(s_4=+2\). The received symbol is \(Y=S+W.\) \(W\) is a zero-mean unit-variance Gaussian random variable and is independent of \(S\). \(P_i\) is the conditional probability of symbol error for the maximum likelihood (ML) decoding when the transmitted symbol \(S=s_i\). The index \(i\) for which the conditional symbol error probability \(P_i\) is the highest is .
questions.explanation: Given \[S_1=-3,\qquad S_2=-1,\qquad S_3=+1,\qquad S_4=+2\] \[Y=S+W\] \[W \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)\] \[f_W(w)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,e^{-w^2/2}\] [figure unavailable] Theory: Since all symbols are equally likely, the optimum decision boundaries are located at the midpoints between adjacent symbols. \[\text{Boundary between }S_1\text{ and }S_2 = \frac{-3+(-1)}{2} = -2\] \[\text{Boundary between }S_2\text{ and }S_3 = \frac{-1+1}{2} = 0\] \[\text{Boundary between }S_3\text{ and }S_4 = \frac{1+2}{2} = 1.5\]Hence, \[S_1:\quad (-\infty,-2)\] \[S_2:\quad (-2,0)\] \[S_3:\quad (0,1.5)\] \[S_4:\quad (1.5,\infty)\] Probability of correct detection regions For \(S_1\), any received value below \(-2\) is decoded correctly. \[P(\text{correct}\mid S_1) = P(Y<-2\mid S_1)\]For \(S_2\), the correct region is between \(-2\) and \(0\). \[P(\text{correct}\mid S_2) = P(-2<Y<0\mid S_2)\]For \(S_3\), the correct region is between \(0\) and \(1.5\). \[P(\text{correct}\mid S_3) = P(0<Y<1.5\mid S_3)\]For \(S_4\), the correct region is greater than \(1.5\). \[P(\text{correct}\mid S_4) = P(Y>1.5\mid S_4)\] Observe that the decision interval for \(S_3\) is the narrowest among all symbols. \[\text{Width of region for }S_3 = 1.5-0 = 1.5\] Therefore, \[P(\text{correct}\mid S_3)\] is the smallest, which implies that \[P(\text{error}\mid S_3)\] is the largest. \[\boxed{S_3\ \text{has the highest conditional symbol error probability}}\]

questions.question: The magnetic field of a uniform plane wave in vacuum is given by \[\vec{H} (x, y, z, t) = (\hat{a}_x + 2\hat{a}_y + b\hat{a}_z) \cos(\omega t + 3x - y - z)\] The value of \(b\) is ________.
questions.explanation:
For a uniform plane wave, the magnetic field intensity vector is perpendicular to the direction of power flow. Let \(\hat{a}_{H}\) be the unit vector in the direction of the magnetic field and \(\hat{a}_{\rho}\) be the unit vector in the direction of power flow. The orthogonality condition is given by: \[\hat{a}_{H} \cdot \hat{a}_{\rho} = 0\] Given the vectors from the problem: \[\hat{a}_{H} = \frac{1\hat{a}_{x} + 2\hat{a}_{y} + b\hat{a}_{z}}{\sqrt{1^{2} + 2^{2} + b^{2}}}\] \[\hat{a}_{\rho} = \frac{-3\hat{a}_{x} + \hat{a}_{y} + \hat{a}_{z}}{\sqrt{3^{2} + 1^{2} + 1^{2}}}\] Applying the dot product to the numerator components (since the product of the magnitudes is non-zero): \[(\hat{a}_{x} + 2\hat{a}_{y} + b\hat{a}_{z}) \cdot (-3\hat{a}_{x} + \hat{a}_{y} + \hat{a}_{z}) = 0\] \[(1)(-3) + (2)(1) + (b)(1) = 0\] \[-3 + 2 + b = 0\] \[b = 1\] \[\boxed{1}\]
Key points
  • In a uniform plane wave (UPW), the electric field \(\vec{E}\), magnetic field \(\vec{H}\), and direction of propagation \(\vec{k}\) (or power flow \(\vec{P}\)) are mutually orthogonal.
  • The dot product of two orthogonal vectors is always zero.

questions.explanation:
For a given reactive impedance (purely imaginary), the impedance is represented as \(Z = jX\). The normalized impedance \(z\) with respect to the characteristic impedance \(Z_{0}\) is given by: \[z = \frac{Z}{Z_{0}} = \frac{jX}{Z_{0}}\] Since \(Z = 0 + jX\), the normalized resistance \(r\) is: \[r = \text{Re}\{z\} = 0\] The complex reflection coefficient \(\Gamma\) is related to the normalized impedance \(z\) by the transformation: \[\Gamma = \frac{z - 1}{z + 1}\] Substituting \(z = jx\) (where \(x = X/Z_{0}\) is the normalized reactance): \[\Gamma = \frac{jx - 1}{jx + 1}\] To find the magnitude \(|\Gamma|\): \[|\Gamma| = \left| \frac{jx - 1}{jx + 1} \right| = \frac{|jx - 1|}{|jx + 1|} = \frac{\sqrt{x^{2} + (-1)^{2}}}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 1^{2}}} = 1\] Because the magnitude of the reflection coefficient is unity (\(|\Gamma| = 1\)) for any value of \(x\) ranging from \(-\infty\) to \(\infty\), the locus of all such points on the complex \(\Gamma\)-plane describes a unit circle centered at the origin \((0, 0)\). \[\boxed{(D):\text{Unit circle}}\]
Key points
  • Purely reactive loads (\(r=0\)) result in total reflection, represented by points on the periphery of the Smith Chart.
  • The transformation from the \(z\)-plane to the \(\Gamma\)-plane maps the imaginary axis of the \(z\)-plane (\(r=0\)) to the unit circle \(|\Gamma|=1\) in the \(\Gamma\)-plane.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not confuse the normalized resistance \(r\) with the reflection coefficient magnitude \(|\Gamma|\). While \(r=0\) describes the vertical axis of the complex impedance plane, it maps to the circular boundary of the reflection coefficient plane.

questions.subject: electromagnetic-fields
questions.question: A transmission line of length \(3\lambda / 4\) and having a characteristic impedance of \(50\ \Omega\) is terminated with a load of \(400\ \Omega\). The impedance (rounded off to two decimal places) seen at the input end of the transmission line is \(\rule{1cm}{0.15mm}\ \Omega\).
questions.explanation:
To find the input impedance \(Z_{in}\) for a transmission line with length \(l = 3\lambda/4\), we use the general formula for the input impedance of a lossless transmission line: [figure unavailable] \[Z_{in} = Z_{0} \left( \frac{Z_{L} + jZ_{0}\tan(\beta l)}{Z_{0} + jZ_{L}\tan(\beta l)} \right)\] Given that \(\beta = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\) and \(l = \frac{3\lambda}{4}\): \[\beta l = \left( \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \right) \left( \frac{3\lambda}{4} \right) = \frac{3\pi}{2}\] Since \(\tan(3\pi/2) \to \infty\), we can rewrite the expression by dividing the numerator and denominator by \(\tan(\beta l)\): \[Z_{in} = Z_{0} \left( \frac{\frac{Z_{L}}{\tan(\beta l)} + jZ_{0}}{\frac{Z_{0}}{\tan(\beta l)} + jZ_{L}} \right)\] As \(\tan(\beta l) \to \infty\): \[Z_{in} = Z_{0} \left( \frac{0 + jZ_{0}}{0 + jZ_{L}} \right) = \frac{Z_{0}^{2}}{Z_{L}}\] This shows that a \(3\lambda/4\) line acts as a \(\lambda/4\) transformer. Substituting the given values \(Z_{0} = 50\,\Omega\) and \(Z_{L} = 400\,\Omega\): \[Z_{in} = \frac{50^{2}}{400} = \frac{2500}{400} = \frac{25}{4} = 6.25\,\Omega\] \[\boxed{6.25\,\Omega}\]
Key points
  • Transmission lines repeat their impedance every \(\lambda/2\) length.
  • A line of length \(l = n\lambda/2 + \lambda/4\) (where \(n\) is an integer) acts as a quarter-wave transformer.
  • The input impedance of a quarter-wave transformer is \(Z_{in} = Z_{0}^{2}/Z_{L}\).

questions.subject: electromagnetic-fields
questions.question: For an infinitesimally small dipole in free space, the electric field \(E_\theta\) in the far field is proportional to \((\dfrac{e^{-jkr}}{r}) \sin\theta\), where \(k = 2\pi/\lambda\). A vertical infinitesimally small electric dipole (\(\delta I \ll \lambda\)) is placed at a distance \(h (h > 0)\) above an infinite ideal conducting plane, as shown in the figure. The minimum value of \(h\), for which one of the maxima in the far field radiation pattern occurs at \(\theta = 60^\circ\), is [figure unavailable]
questions.explanation:
The total electric field of a dipole near an infinite conducting plate can be analyzed using image theory. By placing an image source at a distance \(h\) below the plate, the system is equivalent to a two-element array: [figure unavailable] \[|E_{total}| = |E_{single\_element}| \cdot |A.F.|\] For an array of two elements (\(N=2\)), the array factor magnitude is: \[|A.F.| = \left| \frac{\sin(N\frac{\Psi}{2})}{\sin(\frac{\Psi}{2})} \right| = \left| \frac{\sin(2\frac{\Psi}{2})}{\sin(\frac{\Psi}{2})} \right| = \left| \frac{2\sin(\frac{\Psi}{2})\cos(\frac{\Psi}{2})}{\sin(\frac{\Psi}{2})} \right| = 2\left|\cos\left(\frac{\Psi}{2}\right)\right|\] The normalized array factor \(|A.F._N|\) is: \[|A.F._N| = \frac{|A.F.|}{|A.F.|_{max}} = \left|\cos\left(\frac{\Psi}{2}\right)\right|\] Where the phase difference \(\Psi\) for this geometry is: \[\Psi = \beta d \cos\theta = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} (2h) \cos\theta\] Substituting \(\theta = 60^\circ\) (\(\cos 60^\circ = 0.5\)): \[|A.F._N|_{\theta=60^\circ} = \left| \cos\left( \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \cdot h \cdot 0.5 \right) \right| = \left| \cos\left( \frac{\pi h}{\lambda} \right) \right|\] To find the condition for the maximum of the array factor, we set the argument of the cosine function to \(n\pi\): \[\frac{\pi h}{\lambda} = n\pi \implies h = n\lambda\] For the first non-zero minimum distance (\(n=1\)): \[h_{min} = \lambda\] \[\boxed{\lambda}\]
Key points
  • Image theory simplifies the analysis of antennas near conducting planes by replacing the boundary with an image source.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Incorrectly defining the effective distance \(d\) between the source and its image; remember that for a source at height \(h\), the distance to its image is \(2h\).
  • Confusing the condition for maxima (\(\cos \phi = \pm 1\)) with the condition for nulls.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: He is known for his unscrupulous ways. He always sheds ______ tears to deceive people.
questions.explanation: The term crocodile tears refers to hyporite crying. It is a false or insincere display of grief \[\boxed{\text {C) Crocodile}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Jofra Archer, the England fast bowler, is ________ than accurate.
questions.explanation: The sentence requires the use of the comparative degree to compare two entities or states. When two qualities of the same noun are compared, more + positive degree adjective is used. Use ‘more fast’ and not ‘faster’. \[\boxed{\text {A) more fast} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Select the word that fits the analogy: Build : Building :: Grow : _____
questions.explanation:
The relationship between the words provided follows a morphological pattern of converting a verb into its corresponding abstract noun form.
  • Pair 1: Build (Verb) \(\rightarrow\) Building (Noun)
  • Pair 2: Grow (Verb) \(\rightarrow\) Growth (Noun)

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: I do not think you know the case well enough to have opinions. Having said that, I agree with your other point. What does the phrase “having said that” mean in the given text?
options: as opposed to what I have said
in addition to what I have said
contrary to what I have said

options: Funds raised through unwilling contributions on web-based platforms.
Funds raised through large contributions on web-based platforms.
Funds raised through coerced contributions on web-based platforms.
Funds raised through voluntary contributions on web-based platforms.

The word 'willing' in the context of the sentence indicates a voluntary contribution or a readiness to act without compulsion. \[\boxed{\text {D) Funds raised through voluntary contributions on
web-based platforms} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: While I agree _____ his proposal this time, I do not often agree _____ him.
questions.explanation:
The verb "agree" takes different prepositions depending on the object:
  • Agree to: Used when referring to a proposal, plan, or suggestion.
  • Agree with: Used when referring to a person or their opinion.
\[\boxed{ \text {A) to, with} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The recent measures to improve the output would _____ the level of production to our satisfaction.
questions.explanation:
• Increase: Fits the context of improving levels of production.
  • Decrease: Contradicts the intent of "improving" output.
  • Speed: Generally refers to the rate of a process rather than the "level" of production.
  • Equalise: Means to make things uniform, which does not necessarily imply improvement.
\[\boxed{ \text {A) increase }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Select the word that fits the analogy: White: Whitening : : Light: ________
questions.explanation:
The analogy is based on the relationship between an adjective/noun and its corresponding verb form (specifically, the process of making something that quality).
  • White \(\rightarrow\) Whitening: The act of making something white.
  • Light \(\rightarrow\) Lightening: The act of making something lighter in weight or color.
Distinction of similar-sounding words:
  • Lightning: An electrical discharge in the atmosphere.
  • Lighting: The arrangement or equipment of lights.
  • Enlightening: Giving spiritual or intellectual insight.
\[\boxed{ \text {B) Lightening }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Climate change and resilience deal with two aspects -- reduction of sources of non-renewable energy resources and reducing vulnerability of climate change aspects. The terms `mitigation' and `adaptation' are used to refer to these aspects, respectively. Which of the following assertions is best supported by the above information?
options: Mitigation deals with consequences of climate change
Adaptation deals with causes of climate change
Mitigation deals with actions taken to reduce the use of fossil fuels
Adaptation deals with actions taken to combat green-house gas emissions
questions.explanation:
• Mitigation: Refers to the reduction of sources of non-renewable energy resources.
  • Adaptation: Refers to reducing the vulnerability to climate change aspects.
Evaluating the assertions:
  • Option A: Incorrect. Mitigation deals with the reduction of non-renewable energy sources (causes), not just consequences.
  • Option B: Incorrect. Adaptation deals with reducing vulnerability (consequences/responses), not the causes.
  • Option C: Correct. Since mitigation is defined as the reduction of non-renewable energy sources, it directly corresponds to actions taken to reduce the use of fossil fuels.
  • Option D: Incorrect. Combatting greenhouse gas emissions is a form of mitigation, not adaptation.
\[\boxed{ \text {C) Mitigation deals with actions taken to reduce the use of fossil fuels }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award was conferred ____ Mary Kom, a six-time world champion in boxing, recently in a ceremony ____ the Rashtrapati Bhawan (the President's official residence) in New Delhi.
questions.explanation:
• First Blank: The verb "conferred" is typically followed by the preposition "on" or "upon" when referring to a title, degree, or benefit being bestowed. While "to" is occasionally used in general English, "conferred on" is the standard idiomatic expression for awards.
  • Second Blank: When referring to a specific point or location like "the Rashtrapati Bhawan," the preposition "at" is used to denote the venue of the ceremony.
\[\boxed{ \text {C) on, at}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Despite a string of poor performances, the chances of K. L. Rahul's selection in the team are ______.
questions.explanation:
The sentence uses the preposition "Despite," which indicates a contrast between two conditions. One condition is the "string of poor performances," which is a negative context. Therefore, the second part of the sentence must provide a contrasting positive outcome regarding the chances of selection. Among the given options:
  • Slim: Negative (lowers chances).
  • Bright: Positive (high/good chances).
  • Uncertain: Neutral/Negative.
  • Obvious: Neutral/Context-dependent.
Since "bright" is the opposite of the expectation set by "poor performance," it correctly completes the contrastive logic of the sentence. \[\boxed{\text{ B) bright}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Select the word that fits the analogy: Cover : Uncover :: Associate : _________
questions.explanation: To associate means to connect or join something with something else in the mind or in a physical relationship. The prefix "dis-" is often used to form the opposite of a verb, signifying separation or removal. Therefore, the antonym of associate is dissociate, which means to disconnect or separate. \[\boxed{ \text {D) Dissociate} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Hit by floods, the Kharif (summer sown) crops in various parts of the country have been affected. Officials believe that the loss in production of the kharif crops can be recovered in the output of the rabi (winter sown) crops so that the country can achieve its food-grain production target of 291 million tons in the crop year 2019-20 (July-June). They are hopeful that good rains in July-August will help the soil retain moisture for a longer period, helping winter sown crops such as wheat and pulses during the November-February period. Which of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage?
options: Officials want the food-grain production target to be met by the November-February period.
Officials feel that the food-grain production target cannot be met due to floods.
Officials declared that the food-grain production target will be met due to good rains.
Officials hope that the food-grain production target will be met due to good rabi produce.
questions.explanation: The passage indicates that officials are optimistic about the impact of good rains during the July-August period. This weather pattern is expected to facilitate the recovery of losses over a longer duration. From this context, it can be inferred that the primary hope of the officials is that the food grain production targets will be achieved. This expectation is specifically tied to a successful Rabi produce season following the beneficial rainfall. \[\boxed{\text{D) Officials hope that the food-grain production target will be met due to good rabi produce.} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Repo rate is the rate at which Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends commercial banks, and reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks. Which of the following statements can be inferred from the above passage?
options: Decrease in repo rate will increase cost of borrowing and decrease lending by commercial banks.
Increase in repo rate will decrease cost of borrowing and increase lending by commercial banks.
Increase in repo rate will decrease cost of borrowing and decrease lending by commercial banks.
Decrease in repo rate will decrease cost of borrowing and increase lending by commercial banks.
