The decrease in repo rate increases the flow of money in the economy, hence, increase leading by commercial banks and decrease cost of borrowing. \[\boxed{\text { D) Decrease in repo rate will decrease cost of borrowing and increase lending by commercial banks.} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: He was not only accused of theft _____ of conspiracy.
questions.explanation:
• The phrase "not only" is a correlative conjunction that must always be paired with "but also" to maintain grammatical parallelism.
  • In the given sentence, "He was not only accused of theft of conspiracy," the second part must complete the pair to show that both accusations apply to the subject.
\[\boxed{\text{B) but also} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Select the word that fits the analogy: Explicit: Implicit :: Express: _______
questions.explanation:
The analogy is based on opposite meanings (antonyms).
  • Explicit means openly and clearly expressed.
  • Implicit means implied or hidden; the opposite of explicit.
  • Express means to state or show something openly.
  • Repress means to suppress or hold back; the opposite of express.
Verifying the other options:
  • Impress -- to make an impact; not an antonym of express.
  • Compress -- to press together; not an antonym of express.
  • Suppress -- close in meaning to repress, but ``suppress'' typically refers to forcibly putting down, whereas ``repress'' is the direct antonym of ``express'' (to express vs. to repress feelings).
\[\text{Explicit} : \text{Implicit} \;::\; \text{Express} : \textbf{Repress}\] \[\boxed{\text{B) Repress} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The global financial crisis in 2008 is considered to be the most serious world-wide financial crisis, which started with the sub-prime lending crisis in USA in 2007. The sub-prime lending crisis led to the banking crisis in 2008 with the collapse of Lehman Brothers in 2008. The sub-prime lending refers to the provision of loans to those borrowers who may have difficulties in repaying loans, and it arises because of excess liquidity following the East Asian crisis. Which one of the following sequences shows the correct precedence as per the given passage?
options: East Asian crisis\(\rightarrow\) subprime lending crisis \(\rightarrow\) banking crisis\(\rightarrow\) global financial crisis.
Subprime lending crisis\(\rightarrow\) global financial crisis\(\rightarrow\) banking crisis\(\rightarrow\) East Asian crisis.
Banking crisis\(\rightarrow\) subprime lending crisis\(\rightarrow\) global financial crisis \(\rightarrow\) East Asian crisis.
Global financial crisis \(\rightarrow\) East Asian crisis \(\rightarrow\) banking crisis \(\rightarrow\) subprime lending crisis.
questions.explanation:
The question requires identifying the chronological sequence of events as described in the provided passage. We can determine the precedence by extracting the causal links and years mentioned:
  • Event 1: The passage states that sub-prime lending "arises because of excess liquidity following the East Asian crisis." This places the East Asian crisis at the beginning of the timeline.
  • Event 2: The sub-prime lending crisis started in the USA in 2007.
  • Event 3: The sub-prime lending crisis "led to the banking crisis in 2008 with the collapse of Lehman Brothers."
  • Event 4: The passage identifies the global financial crisis of 2008 as the overall result of these preceding events.
The correct chronological sequence is: \[\text{East Asian crisis} \to \text{subprime lending crisis} \to \text{banking crisis} \to \text{global financial crisis}\] \[\boxed{\text{A) East Asian crisis$\rightarrow$ subprime lending crisis $\rightarrow$ banking crisis$\rightarrow$ global financial crisis.} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: This book, including all its chapters, ____ interesting. The students as well as the instructor ____ in agreement about it.
questions.explanation:
Case 1: "This book, including all its chapters, _____ interesting."
  • Verb Selection: Since the subject is singular, the verb must be singular: is.
Case 2: "The students as well as the instructor _____ in agreement about it."
  • Verb Selection: Since the first noun "The students" is plural, the verb must be plural: are.
\[\boxed{\text{C) is, are} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: People were prohibited __________ their vehicles near the entrance of the main administrative building.
questions.explanation:
• Verb Form: When a verb follows the preposition "from", it must be in the gerund form (verb + ing).
  • Construction: Subject + be + prohibited + from + v-ing.
\[\boxed{\text{B) from parking} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Select the word that fits the analogy: Do : Undo :: Trust : _______
questions.explanation:
• Do : Undo: The word "Undo" is the direct antonym (opposite) of "Do," formed by adding the negative prefix un-. The relationship is "Action : Reversal/Opposite of Action."
  • Trust : _____: To maintain the analogy, we must find the standard antonym for the word "Trust."
  • Distrust: Correct. This is the standard English antonym for trust, indicating a lack of trust or suspicion.
\[\text{Do} : \text{Undo} :: \text{Trust} : \boxed{\text{C) Distrust}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Stock markets _______ at the news of the coup.
questions.explanation:
Evaluation of Options:
  • (a) poised: To be balanced or suspended; or to be ready for action. It does not describe the reaction to a negative event.
  • (b) plunged: To fall suddenly and uncontrollably. In financial terms, this specifically describes a sharp, rapid decline in value. This is the most contextually appropriate word.
  • (c) plugged: To block or fill a hole; or to promote something. It does not relate to market movement.
  • (d) probed: To physically explore or examine something with a tool; or to investigate. Markets do not "probe" at news in this grammatical structure.
\[\boxed{\text{B) plunged} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Non-performing Assets (NPAs) of a bank in India is defined as an asset, which remains unpaid by a borrower for a certain period of time in terms of interest, principal, or both. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has changed the definition of NPA thrice during 1993-2004, in terms of the holding period of loans. The holding period was reduced by one quarter each time. In 1993, the holding period was four quarters (360 days). Based on the above paragraph, the holding period of loans in 2004 after the third revision was _______ days.
questions.explanation:
The problem requires a step-by-step reduction of the holding period for Non-performing Assets (NPAs) based on the conditions provided in the paragraph. Initial State (1993):
  • Holding Period = \(4\) quarters.
  • Total Days = \(360\) days.
  • Days per quarter = \(\frac{360}{4} = 90\) days.
Reduction Logic:
The RBI changed the definition thrice, reducing the holding period by one quarter each time. Step-by-Step Calculation:
  1. First Revision:
    \[4 \text{ quarters} - 1 \text{ quarter} = 3 \text{ quarters}\] \[3 \times 90 \text{ days} = 270 \text{ days}\]
  2. Second Revision:
    \[3 \text{ quarters} - 1 \text{ quarter} = 2 \text{ quarters}\] \[2 \times 90 \text{ days} = 180 \text{ days}\]
  3. Third Revision (Final):
    \[2 \text{ quarters} - 1 \text{ quarter} = 1 \text{ quarter}\] \[1 \times 90 \text{ days} = 90 \text{ days}\]
Thus, the holding period in 2004 after the third revision was \(90\) days. \[\boxed{\text {B) 90}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Select the next element of the series: Z, WV, RQP, ____
questions.explanation:
1. First Element: Z
    • Number of letters: \(1\)
    • Alphabet position: \(26\)
  2. Second Element: WV
    • Number of letters: \(2\)
    • Alphabet positions: \(23, 22\)
  3. Third Element: RQP
    • Number of letters: \(3\)
    • Alphabet positions: \(18, 17, 16\)
  4. Fourth Element: ?
    • Gap Pattern: The gap increases by one each time (\(2, 3 \rightarrow\) next gap should be \(4\)).
    • Next starting letter: \(16 - 4 - 1 = 11\) (Letter K).
    • Quantity Pattern: The number of letters increases by one (\(1, 2, 3 \rightarrow\) next element should have \(4\) letters).
    • Alphabet positions: \(11, 10, 9, 8\) (K, J, I, H).
\[\text{Series: Z, WV, RQP, } \boxed{\text{KJIH}}\] \[\boxed{\text{C) KJIH} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Raman is confident of speaking English _____ six months as he has been practising regularly _____ the last three weeks.
questions.explanation:
The complete sentence is: "Raman is confident of speaking English within six months as he has been practising regularly for the last three weeks." \[\boxed{\text{D) within, for} }\]
Key points
  • For vs. Since: Use 'for' for a duration (e.g., for 3 weeks, for 5 hours) and 'since' for a specific point in time (e.g., since Monday, since 2010).
  • Within: Indicates a limit; something happening before a specific time period expires.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: His knowledge of the subject was excellent but his classroom performance was ______.
questions.explanation:
The sentence: "His knowledge of the subject was excellent but his classroom performance was extremely poor."
  • The logic behind selecting the correct option is based on the use of the coordinating conjunction 'but':
  • The word 'but' is used to introduce a phrase or clause that contrasts with what has already been mentioned.
\[\boxed{\text {A) extremely poor}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Select the word that fits the analogy: Cook : Cook :: Fly : ______
questions.explanation:
• Cook : Cook :: One who performs the act of cooking is called a cook.
  • Fly : Flyer :: Similarly, one who performs the act of flying (an aircraft or generally) is called a flyer.
\[\boxed{\text{A) Flyer} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Goods and Services Tax (GST) is an indirect tax introduced in India in 2017 that is imposed on the supply of goods and services, and it subsumes all indirect taxes except few. It is a destination-based tax imposed on goods and services used, and it is not imposed at the point of origin from where goods come. GST also has a few components specific to state governments, central government and Union Territories (UTs). Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage?
options: GST is imposed on the production of goods and services.
GST does not have a component specific to UT.
GST is imposed at the point of usage of goods and services.
questions.explanation:
To identify the correct inference regarding Goods and Services Tax (GST), we evaluate each option against the passage text:
  • Option (a): The passage states GST is imposed on the supply of goods and services. Production (manufacturing) is different from supply, making this incorrect.
  • Option (b): The passage explicitly mentions that GST has components specific to "Union Territories (UTs)." Therefore, saying it does not have such a component is false.
  • Option (c): The text describes GST as a "destination-based tax" that is "not imposed at the point of origin." This implies it is imposed where the goods/services are consumed or used. This statement is a valid inference.
  • Option (d): The passage states GST subsumes all indirect taxes "except few." Therefore, it does not include all indirect taxes.
\[\boxed{\text{D) GST is imposed at the point of usage of goods and services.} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: It is a common criticism that most of the academicians live in their ______, so, they are not aware of the real life challenges.
questions.explanation:
• The idiom 'ivory tower' refers to a state of privileged seclusion or separation from the facts and practicalities of the real world.
  • In this context, the criticism directed at academicians is that their intellectual environment keeps them disconnected from "real life challenges."
  • The other options (glass palaces, big flats, homes) are literal descriptions of dwellings and do not carry the metaphorical meaning of being out of touch with reality.
\[\boxed{ \text{B) ivory towers}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: His hunger for reading is insatiable. He reads indiscriminately. He is most certainly a/an _____ reader.
questions.explanation: The term voracious is specifically used to describe an engaging activity (like reading or eating) performed with great eagerness or an appetite that is difficult to satisfy. \[\boxed{ \text{C) voracious}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Select the word that fits the analogy: Fuse : Fusion :: Use : ______
questions.explanation:
Analyze the first pair: Fuse : Fusion
  • Fuse is a verb meaning to join or blend to form a single entity.
  • Fusion is the noun form representing the process or result of fusing.
Apply the same logic to the second pair: Use : ?
  • Use is a verb meaning to take, hold, or deploy something as a means of accomplishing a purpose.
  • The standard noun form that describes the action or manner of using something is Usage.
Thus, the analogy is completed as Fuse : Fusion :: Use : Usage. \[\boxed{\text{A) Usage} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The American psychologist Howard Gardner expounds that human intelligence can be sub-categorised into multiple kinds, in such a way that individuals differ with respect to their relative competence in each kind. Based on this theory, modern educationists insist on prescribing multi-dimensional curriculum and evaluation parameters that enable development and assessment of multiple intelligences. Which of the following statements can be inferred from the given text?
options: Howard Gardner insists that the teaching curriculum and evaluation needs to be multi-dimensional.
Howard Gardner wants to develop and assess the theory of multiple intelligences.
Modern educationists want to develop and assess the theory of multiple intelligences.
Modern educationists insist that the teaching curriculum and evaluation needs to be multi-dimensional.
questions.explanation:
Deconstruct the passage to identify the roles and actions of each party mentioned:
  • Howard Gardner: Expounds the theory that human intelligence is sub-categorized into multiple kinds and that individuals differ in their competence in each.
  • Modern Educationists: Based on Gardner's theory, they are the ones who insist on prescribing multi-dimensional curriculum and evaluation parameters.
Evaluating the options:
  • A: Incorrect. The text states modern educationists insist on this, not necessarily Gardner himself.
  • B: Incorrect. The text does not state Gardner's current desires regarding the development of the theory; it only describes his core premise.
  • C: Incorrect. Educationists want to develop and assess the multiple intelligences of individuals, not the theory itself.
  • D: Correct. This directly aligns with the second sentence of the text, which states that modern educationists insist on multi-dimensional curriculum and evaluation.
\[\boxed{\text{D) Modern educationists insist that the teaching curriculum and evaluation needs to be multi-dimensional.} }\]

questions.question: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T went camping. At night, they had to sleep in a row inside the tent. P, Q and T refused to sleep next to R since he snored loudly.     • \(Q\) is next to \(T\) (Allowed; \(T\) is not \(P\) or \(S\)).
    • Result: Valid.
  • B: SPRTQ
    • \(R\) is next to \(P\) (Violates Constraint 1).
    • Result: Invalid.
  • C: QTSPR
    • \(R\) is next to \(P\) (Violates Constraint 1).
    • Result: Invalid.

    • \(R\) is next to \(Q\) (Violates Constraint 1).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word that can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. Now-a-days, most children have a tendency to <u>belittle</u> the legitimate concerns of their parents.
questions.explanation:
The objective is to identify the synonym for the word belittle that fits the context of the sentence.

  • Disparage: To represent something as being of little worth; to depreciate. This is a direct synonym for belittle.
  • Applaud: To express strong approval (Antonym).
  • Reduce: To make smaller in size or amount; while related to "making little," it does not carry the same connotation of social dismissal as belittle.
  • Begrudge: To envy someone the possession of something; to give reluctantly.
Both belittle and disparage convey the sense of devaluing someone's opinions or concerns. \[\boxed{\text{A) disparage} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Nominal interest rate is defined as the amount paid by the borrower to the lender for using the borrowed amount for a specific period of time. Real interest rate calculated on the basis of actual value (inflation-adjusted), is approximately equal to the difference between nominal rate and expected rate of inflation in the economy. Which of the following assertions is best supported by the above information?
options: Under high inflation, real interest rate is low and borrowers get benefited.
Under low inflation, real interest rate is high and borrowers get benefited.
Under high inflation, real interest rate is low and lenders get benefited.
Under low inflation, real interest rate is low and borrowers get benefited.
questions.explanation:
The relationship between the nominal interest rate, the real interest rate, and inflation is governed by the Fisher Equation. 1. The Formula
The approximate relationship is expressed as: \[r \approx i - \pi\] Where:
  • \(r\) is the real interest rate (the actual purchasing power gained or lost).
  • \(i\) is the nominal interest rate (the stated percentage on a loan or investment).
  • \(\pi\) is the inflation rate (the rate at which prices increase).
2. Impact of High Inflation
When the inflation rate (\(\pi\)) increases significantly:
  • The real interest rate (\(r\)) decreases (it can even become negative if \(\pi > i\)).
  • Borrowers benefit: They repay their loans with "cheaper" money that has less purchasing power than the money they originally borrowed.
  • Lenders lose: The value of the repayments they receive is eroded by the high inflation.
3. Evaluation of Options
  • Under high inflation, the real interest rate is low, and borrowers get benefitted. This matches our derivation.
\[\boxed{\text{A) Under high inflation, real interest rate is low and borrowers get benefited.} }\]

questions.question: The sum of the first \(n\) terms in the sequence \(8, 88, 888, 8888, \dots\) is ______.
questions.explanation:
To find the sum of the first \(n\) terms in the sequence \(8, 88, 888, 8888, \dots\): \[S = 8 + 88 + 888 + \dots + \text{upto } n \text{ terms}\] \[S = 8(1 + 11 + 111 + \dots + \text{upto } n \text{ terms})\] Multiply and divide by \(9\): \[S = \frac{8}{9} [9 + 99 + 999 + \dots + \text{upto } n \text{ terms}]\] \[S = \frac{8}{9} [(10 - 1) + (100 - 1) + (1000 - 1) + \dots + \text{upto } n \text{ terms}]\] \[S = \frac{8}{9} [(10 + 10^2 + 10^3 + \dots + 10^n) - (1 + 1 + 1 + \dots \text{ upto } n)]\] The first part is a Geometric Progression (G.P.) where \(a = 10\) and \(r = 10\). Using the sum formula \(S_n = \frac{a(r^n - 1)}{r - 1}\): \[S = \frac{8}{9} \left[ \frac{10(10^n - 1)}{10 - 1} - n \right]\] \[S = \frac{8}{9} \left[ \frac{10(10^n - 1)}{9} - n \right]\] \[\boxed {{{\text D) } \frac{80}{81}(10^n - 1) - \frac{8}{9}n}}\]
Key points
  • For sequences with repeating digits, use the "Multiply and Divide by 9" technique to convert them into powers of 10.
  • Sum of a G.P. for \(r > 1\) is \(S_n = \frac{a(r^n - 1)}{r - 1}\).
  • The term \((1+1+1 \dots n \text{ times})\) always simplifies to \(n\).

questions.question: The bar graph shows the data of the students who appeared and passed in an examination for four schools P, Q, R and S. The average of success rates (in percentage) of these four schools is ______.

questions.question: In one of the greatest innings ever seen in \(142\) years of Test history, Ben Stokes upped the tempo in a five-and-a-half hour long stay of \(219\) balls including \(11\) fours and \(8\) sixes that saw him finish on a \(135\) not out as England squared the five-match series. Based on their connotations in the given passage, which one of the following meanings DOES NOT match?
questions.explanation:
• upped = increased: In the context of "upped the tempo," it correctly means he increased the speed or intensity of his play.
  • tempo = enthusiasm: While "tempo" technically refers to speed, in this passage it connotes the energy or enthusiasm with which the innings was played.
  • saw = resulted in: The phrase "saw him finish" implies that the events described resulted in his final score.
  • squared = lost: In sports, to "square a series" means to level the scores or make the series tied (e.g., 1-1 or 2-2). It does not mean to lose.
The meaning "lost" does not match the connotation of "squared." \[\boxed{\text {B) squared = lost} }\]

questions.question: There are five levels \(\{P, Q, R, S, T\}\) in a linear supply chain before a product reaches customers, as shown in the figure. At each of the five levels, the price of the product is increased by \(25\%\). If the product is produced at level \(P\) at the cost of Rs. \(120\) per unit, what is the price paid (in rupees) by the customers?
questions.explanation:
The supply chain is given as: \[P \rightarrow Q \rightarrow R \rightarrow S \rightarrow T \rightarrow \text{Customer}\] There are 5 levels of transfer (\(P\) to \(Q\), \(Q\) to \(R\), \(R\) to \(S\), \(S\) to \(T\), and \(T\) to Customer). At each level, the price increases by \(25\%\). \[\text{Price}_{\text{final}} = \text{Price}_{\text{initial}} \times \left( 1 + \frac{r}{100} \right)^n\] Where:
  • \(\text{Price}_{\text{initial}} = 120\)
  • \(r = 25\%\)
  • \(n = 5\) (number of levels)
Substituting the values: \[\text{Price}_{\text{final}} = 120 \times \frac{125}{100} \times \frac{125}{100} \times \frac{125}{100} \times \frac{125}{100} \times \frac{125}{100}\] \[\text{Price}_{\text{final}} = 120 \times (1.25)^5\] \[\text{Price}_{\text{final}} = 120 \times 3.0517578125\] \[\text{Price}_{\text{final}} = 366.2109375\] \[\boxed{ \text {D) 366.21 }}\]

questions.question: It was estimated that \(52\) men can complete a strip in a newly constructed highway connecting cities \(P\) and \(Q\) in \(10\) days. Due to an emergency, \(12\) men were sent to another project. How many number of days, more than the original estimate, will be required to complete the strip?
questions.explanation: Given that \(52\) men can complete a task in \(10\) days. If \(12\) men are sent out, the number of remaining men is: \[\text{Remaining men} = 52 - 12 = 40\] We use the work-rate principle where the total work remains constant (\(M_1 D_1 = M_2 D_2\)). Let \(x\) be the number of days required by the remaining \(40\) men. \[M_1 D_1 = M_2 D_2\] \[52 \times 10 = 40 \times x\] Solving for \(x\): \[x = \frac{52 \times 10}{40}\] \[x = \frac{520}{40} = 13 \text{ days}\] Total number of days taken is \(13\) days, which is \(3\) days more than the original estimate of \(10\) days. \[\boxed{ \text {A) 3 days}  }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: An engineer measures THREE quantities X, Y and Z in an experiment. She finds that they follow a relationship that is represented in the figure below: (the product of X and Y linearly varies with Z) Then, which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: For fixed Z; X is proportional to Y
For fixed Y; X is proportional to Z
For fixed X; Z is proportional to Y
questions.explanation:
From the given graph, the line passes through the origin \(O\), and the vertical axis represents the product \(X \cdot Y\) while the horizontal axis represents \(Z\). The equation of a straight line passing through the origin is given by: \[X \cdot Y = m \cdot Z\] where \(m\) is the constant slope of the line. From this relationship, we can determine that: \[\frac{X \cdot Y}{Z} = m = \text{constant}\] Now, let's evaluate the given assertions to find the FALSE statement:
  • Option A: For fixed \(Z\), \(X \cdot Y = m \cdot Z = \text{constant}\). This implies \(X \propto \frac{1}{Y}\) (inversely proportional). Therefore, the statement that \(X\) is proportional to \(Y\) is FALSE.
  • Option B: For fixed \(Y\), \(X \cdot Y = m \cdot Z \implies X = \left(\frac{m}{Y}\right) Z\). Thus, \(X \propto Z\). This is true.
  • Option C: For fixed \(X\), \(X \cdot Y = m \cdot Z \implies Y = \left(\frac{m}{X}\right) Z\). Thus, \(Z \propto Y\). This is true.
  • Option D: \(\frac{X \cdot Y}{Z}\) is constant. As derived above, this is true.
\[\boxed{ \text {A) For fixed Z; X is proportional to Y }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The two pie-charts given below show the data of total students and only girls registered in different streams in a university. If the total number of students registered in the university is 5000, and the total number of the registered girls is 1500; then, the ratio of boys enrolled in Arts to the girls enrolled in Management is .
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the number of Boys in Arts
The number of boys in Arts is the total number of students in Arts minus the number of girls in Arts. From the first pie chart, total students in Arts = \(20\%\) of \(5000\). From the second pie chart, girls in Arts = \(30\%\) of \(1500\). \[(\text{Boys})_{\text{Arts}} = (20\% \text{ of } 5000) - (30\% \text{ of } 1500)\] \[(\text{Boys})_{\text{Arts}} = 1000 - 450 = 550\] Step 2: Calculate the number of Girls in Management
From the second pie chart, girls in Management = \(15\%\) of \(1500\). \[(\text{Girls})_{\text{Management}} = 15\% \text{ of } 1500 = 225\] Step 3: Calculate the required ratio
The ratio of boys in Arts to girls in Management is: \[\text{Ratio} = \frac{(\text{Boys})_{\text{Arts}}}{(\text{Girls})_{\text{Management}}} = \frac{550}{225} \ = \frac{22}{9}\] \[\boxed{\text {D) 22 : 9} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The difference between the sum of the first \(2n\) natural numbers and the sum of the first \(n\) odd natural numbers is ___.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Sum of first \(2n\) natural numbers (\(S_{2n}\))
The first \(2n\) natural numbers are \(1, 2, 3, \dots, 2n\). This is an Arithmetic Progression (AP) where the first term \(a = 1\), common difference \(d = 1\), and number of terms is \(2n\). \[S_{2n} = \frac{\text{Number of terms}}{2} [2 \times \text{First term} + (\text{Number of terms} - 1) \times d]\] \[S_{2n} = \frac{2n}{2} [2(1) + (2n - 1)(1)]\] \[S_{2n} = n [2 + 2n - 1] = n(2n + 1) = 2n^2 + n\] Step 2: Sum of first \(n\) odd positive integers (\(S_{odd}\))
The first \(n\) odd positive integers are \(1, 3, 5, \dots, (2n-1)\). Here \(a = 1\), \(d = 2\), and number of terms is \(n\). \[S_{odd} = \frac{n}{2} [2(1) + (n - 1)(2)]\] \[S_{odd} = \frac{n}{2} [2 + 2n - 2] = \frac{n}{2} [2n] = n^2\] Step 3: Calculate the difference
\[\text{Difference} = S_{2n} - S_{odd}\] \[\text{Difference} = (2n^2 + n) - n^2 = n^2 + n\] \[\boxed{n^2 + n}\]
Key points
  • Sum of an Arithmetic Progression: \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a + (n-1)d]\).
  • Sum of first \(k\) natural numbers: \(\frac{k(k+1)}{2}\).
  • Sum of first \(n\) odd natural numbers: \(n^2\).
\[\boxed{\text { B) $n^2 + n$} }\]
Mistakes to avoid
Ensure the number of terms for the natural numbers is correctly identified as \(2n\) and not \(n\). Double-check the common difference for odd integers (\(d=2\)).

questions.question:
\(P, Q, R, S, T, U, V,\) and \(W\) are seated around a circular table.
  1. \(S\) is seated opposite to \(W\).
  2. \(U\) is seated at the second place to the right of \(R\).
  3. \(T\) is seated at the third place to the left of \(R\).
  4. \(V\) is a neighbour of \(S\).
Which of the following must be true?
questions.explanation:
The seating arrangement of \(P\), \(Q\), \(R\), \(S\), \(T\), \(U\), \(V\), and \(W\) around a circular table is analyzed based on the provided diagram. From the figure, the relative positions are as follows:
  • \(S\) is seated at the top position.
  • \(R\) and \(V\) are adjacent to \(S\).
  • \(T\) is seated opposite the position shared by \(P/Q\).
  • \(W\) is seated at the bottom position, opposite \(S\).
  • \(U\) and the second \(P/Q\) position are adjacent to \(W\).
Since \(P\) and \(Q\) occupy positions that are not directly across from one another (they are separated by two other seats in either direction), the statement that must be true is that \(P\) is not seated opposite to \(Q\). \[\boxed{\text{ C) $P$ is not seated opposite to $Q$.} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The distance between Delhi and Agra is \(233\) km. A car \(P\) started travelling from Delhi to Agra and another car \(Q\) started from Agra to Delhi along the same road \(1\) hour after the car \(P\) started. The two cars crossed each other \(75\) minutes after the car \(Q\) started. Both cars were travelling at constant speed. The speed of car \(P\) was \(10\) km/hr more than the speed of car \(Q\). How many kilometers the car \(Q\) had travelled when the cars crossed each other?
questions.explanation: Given that the distance between Delhi and Agra is \(233\,\text{km}\). Car \(P\) starts from Delhi and Car \(Q\) starts from Agra toward each other. They cross each other \(75\,\text{minutes}\) after Car \(Q\) started. Let \(x\,\text{km}\) be the distance covered by Car \(Q\) in \(75\,\text{minutes}\). \[\text{Time taken by Car } Q = 75\,\text{min} = \frac{75}{60}\,\text{hr} = \frac{5}{4}\,\text{hr}\] \[\text{Speed of Car } Q = \frac{x}{5/4} = \frac{4x}{5}\,\text{km/hr}\] From the problem context, the speed of Car \(P\) is \(10\,\text{km/hr}\) more than Car \(Q\): \[\text{Speed of Car } P = \left( \frac{4x}{5} + 10 \right)\,\text{km/hr}\] Car \(P\) had been traveling for \(1\,\text{hr}\) and \(75\,\text{min}\) before crossing: \[\text{Time for Car } P = 1\,\text{hr} + 75\,\text{min} = 1 + \frac{5}{4} = \frac{9}{4}\,\text{hr}\] The distance covered by Car \(P\) till the point of crossing is \((233 - x)\,\text{km}\). \[\text{Distance} = \text{Speed} \times \text{Time}\] \[(233 - x) = \frac{9}{4} \left( \frac{4x}{5} + 10 \right)\] \[233 - x = \frac{9}{4} \times \frac{4x}{5} + \frac{9}{4} \times 10\] \[233 - x = \frac{9x}{5} + 22.5\] \[233 - 22.5 = \frac{9x}{5} + x\] \[210.5 = \frac{14x}{5}\] \[x = \frac{210.5 \times 5}{14} \approx 75.178\,\text{km}\] Rounding to the provided solution value: \[x \approx 75.2\,\text{km}\] \[\boxed{ \text {B) 75.2} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: For a matrix \(M = [m_{ij}]; i,j = 1,2,3,4\), the diagonal elements are all zero and \(m_{ij} = -m_{ji}\). The minimum number of elements required to fully specify the matrix is ____.
questions.explanation:
Given the matrix \(M = [m_{ij}]\) for \(i, j = 1, 2, 3, 4\), where the diagonal elements are all zero and \(m_{ij} = -m_{ji}\). This definition characterizes a skew-symmetric matrix. The matrix can be represented as: \[M = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & m_{12} & m_{13} & m_{14} \\ -m_{12} & 0 & m_{23} & m_{24} \\ -m_{13} & -m_{23} & 0 & m_{34} \\ -m_{14} & -m_{24} & -m_{34} & 0 \end{bmatrix}\] In a skew-symmetric matrix of order \(n \times n\):
  • The diagonal elements must be zero (\(m_{ii} = 0\)).
  • The elements above the diagonal determine the elements below the diagonal due to the property \(m_{ij} = -m_{ji}\).
The number of elements required to fully specify such a matrix is equivalent to the number of elements above (or below) the principal diagonal. For an \(n \times n\) matrix, this is calculated as: \[\text{Number of independent elements} = \frac{n^2 - n}{2}\] For \(n = 4\): \[\frac{4^2 - 4}{2} = \frac{16 - 4}{2} = 6\] Thus, the minimum number of elements required is 6. \[\boxed{ \text {B) 6} }\]
Key points
  • A skew-symmetric matrix satisfies \(M^T = -M\).
  • The diagonal elements of any skew-symmetric matrix are always zero.
  • For an \(n \times n\) skew-symmetric matrix, there are \(\frac{n(n-1)}{2}\) independent non-zero elements.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not count the diagonal elements, as they are fixed at zero.
  • Do not count all non-diagonal elements (\(n^2 - n\)); remember that \(m_{ij}\) and \(m_{ji}\) are dependent on each other.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The profit shares of two companies P and Q are shown in the figure. If the two companies have invested a fixed and equal amount every year, then the ratio of the total revenue of company P to the total revenue of company Q, during 2013 - 2018 is ________.
questions.explanation: Based on the provided information, the relationship between revenue, profit, and investment is defined as: \[\text{Revenue} = \text{Profit} + \text{Investment}\] Assuming a base investment of \(100\) units for both companies, the total revenue is calculated by summing the (Investment + Profit) for each period provided in the data. For Company \(P\):\[\text{Total Revenue}_P = (100+10) + (100+20) + (100+40) + (100+40) + (100+50) + (100+40)\] \[\text{Total Revenue}_P = 110 + 120 + 140 + 140 + 150 + 140 = 800\] For Company \(Q\): \[\text{Total Revenue}_Q = (100+20) + (100+30) + (100+30) + (100+50) + (100+60) + (100+60)\] \[\text{Total Revenue}_Q = 120 + 130 + 130 + 150 + 160 + 160 = 850\] The ratio of total revenue of Company \(P\) to Company \(Q\) is: \[\frac{\text{Total Revenue}_P}{\text{Total Revenue}_Q} = \frac{800}{850} = \frac{16}{17}\] \[\boxed{ \text {B) 16:17}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The untimely loss of life is a cause of serious global concern as thousands of people get killed _____ accidents every year while many other die _____ diseases like cardio vascular disease, cancer, etc.
questions.explanation:
• First Blank: When referring to death resulting from a specific event or circumstance like an accident, the preposition 'in' is used (e.g., killed in an accident).
  • Second Blank: When referring to death caused by a disease, the standard preposition is 'of' (e.g., die of cancer, die of a heart attack).
\[\boxed{\text{ A) in, of} }\]
Key points
  • Use 'in' for accidents, wars, or specific catastrophic events.
  • Use 'of' for internal causes like diseases, hunger, or thirst.
  • Use 'from' for external causes like exhaustion, wounds, or overeating.
Mistakes to avoid
Do not confuse 'die of' with 'die from'. While sometimes used interchangeably in casual speech, formal grammar distinguishes between direct internal causes (of) and indirect/external causes (from).

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The Canadian constitution requires that equal importance be given to English and French. Last year, Air Canada lost a lawsuit, and had to pay a six-figure fine to a French-speaking couple after they filed complaints about formal in-flight announcements in English lasting 15 seconds, as opposed to informal 5 second messages in French. The French-speaking couple were upset at ________.
options: the in-flight announcements being made in English.
the English announcements being clearer than the French ones.

questions.question: A superadditive function \(f(\cdot)\) satisfies the following property \[f(x_1 + x_2) \ge f(x_1) + f(x_2)\] Which of the following functions is a superadditive function for \(x > 1\)?
questions.explanation:
A function \(f(x)\) is defined as superadditive if it satisfies the following property for all \(x_{1}, x_{2}\) in its domain: \[f(x_{1} + x_{2}) \geq f(x_{1}) + f(x_{2})\] Let's evaluate the given options for \(x > 1\):
  • Option (a): \(f(x) = e^{x}\). Since \(e > 1\), the exponential function grows faster than the sum of its parts. For \(x_{1}, x_{2} > 0\): \[e^{x_{1} + x_{2}} = e^{x_{1}} \cdot e^{x_{2}}\] For \(x > 1\), \(e^{x} > 2\), so \(e^{x_{1}} \cdot e^{x_{2}} > e^{x_{1}} + e^{x_{2}}\) is generally satisfied.
  • Option (b): \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\). This is a concave function. For concave functions where \(f(0) \geq 0\), the relationship is \(f(x_{1} + x_{2}) \leq f(x_{1}) + f(x_{2})\), making it subadditive.
  • Option (c): \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x}\). For \(x_{1}=2, x_{2}=3\), \(f(2+3) = \frac{1}{5} = 0.2\), while \(f(2)+f(3) = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{5}{6} \approx 0.833\). Since \(0.2 < 0.833\), it is subadditive.
  • Option (d): \(f(x) = e^{-x}\). This is a decaying function, similar to \(1/x\), and will be subadditive.
As shown in the example: \[2^{5} > 2^{2} + 2^{3} \implies 32 > 4 + 8\] Since \(e > 1\), \(f(x) = e^{x}\) satisfies the superadditive property. \[\boxed{\text {A) $e^x$}}\]

questions.question: It is quarter past three in your watch. The angle between the hour hand and the minute hand is _____.
questions.explanation:
The time "quarter past three" corresponds to 03:15. We need to find the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at this specific time.
Method 1
Using the standard clock angle formula: \[\theta = \left| 30h - \frac{11m}{2} \right|\] Where \(h\) is the hour and \(m\) is the minutes. Given \(h = 3\) and \(m = 15\): \[\theta = \left| 30(3) - \frac{11(15)}{2} \right|\] \[\theta = \left| 90 - \frac{165}{2} \right|\] \[\theta = | 90 - 82.5 | = 7.5^\circ\]
Method 2
Alternatively, consider the movement of each hand from the 12 o'clock position:
  • Minute Hand: At 15 minutes, it is exactly at the 3 mark. Angle = \(15 \times 6^\circ = 90^\circ\).
  • Hour Hand: At 3:15, the hour hand has moved slightly past the 3 mark due to the 15 minutes elapsed. \[\text{Angle} = (3 \times 30^\circ) + (15 \times 0.5^\circ) = 90^\circ + 7.5^\circ = 97.5^\circ\]
  • Difference: \(|97.5^\circ - 90^\circ| = 7.5^\circ\).
\[\boxed{ \text{B) $7.5^{\circ}$}}\]
Key points
  • The hour hand moves \(0.5^\circ\) per minute.
  • The minute hand moves \(6^\circ\) per minute.
  • The relative speed between the hands is \(5.5^\circ\) per minute.
Mistakes to avoid
A common mistake is assuming the angle is \(0^\circ\) because both hands appear to be at "3". Remember that the hour hand is not stationary; it moves continuously as the minutes pass.

questions.question: A circle with centre O is shown in the figure. A rectangle PQRS of maximum possible area is inscribed in the circle. If the radius of the circle is \(a\), then the area of the shaded portion is _____.
questions.explanation:
The objective is to find the maximum possible area of a rectangle inscribed within a circle of radius \(a\). Based on the geometric principles of optimization:
  • For a fixed perimeter or a fixed bounding shape (like a circle), the area of an inscribed rectangle is maximized when the rectangle is a square.
  • The diagonal of this square must be equal to the diameter of the circle. Since the radius is \(a\), the diagonal is \(d = 2a\).
The area of the square can be calculated using its diagonal: \[\text{Area of square} = \frac{1}{2} \times (\text{diagonal})^2\] \[\text{Area of square} = \frac{1}{2} \times (2a)^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 4a^2 = 2a^2\] Now, we calculate the area of the shaded portion, which represents the region inside the circle but outside the maximum rectangle (the square): \[\text{Area of shaded portion} = \text{Area of circle} - \text{Area of square}\] \[\text{Area of circle} = \pi a^2\] \[\text{Area of shaded portion} = \pi a^2 - 2a^2\] \[\boxed{\text{C) $\pi a^2 - 2a^2$} }\]

questions.question: \(a, b, c\) are real numbers. The quadratic equation \(ax^2 - bx + c = 0\) has equal roots, which is \(\beta\), then
questions.explanation:
Given the quadratic equation: \[ax^{2} - bx + c = 0\] Since the equation has equal roots, both roots are \(\beta\). We can use the relationships between roots and coefficients for a quadratic equation of the form \(Ax^{2} + Bx + C = 0\):
  • Sum of roots:
    \[\beta + \beta = -\frac{(-b)}{a} \implies 2\beta = \frac{b}{a} \quad \dots(1)\]
  • Product of roots:
    \[\beta \cdot \beta = \frac{c}{a} \implies \beta^{2} = \frac{c}{a} \quad \dots(2)\]
To find the expression for \(\beta^{3}\), we multiply equation (1) by equation (2): \[(2\beta)(\beta^{2}) = \left( \frac{b}{a} \right) \left( \frac{c}{a} \right)\] \[2\beta^{3} = \frac{bc}{a^{2}}\] \[\beta^{3} = \frac{bc}{2a^{2}}\] \[\boxed{ \text{C) $\beta^3 = bc/(2a^2)$}}\]

questions.question: The following figure shows the data of students enrolled in 5 years (2014 to 2018) for two schools P and Q. During this period, the ratio of the average number of the students enrolled in school P to the average of the difference of the number of students enrolled in schools P and Q is
questions.explanation:
The problem requires calculating a ratio based on the enrollment data for two schools, P and Q, over a 5-year period (2014 to 2018).
  • Step 1: Calculate the average number of students enrolled in school P.
    The enrollments for school P are \(3000, 5000, 5000, 6000,\) and \(4000\). \[\text{Average}_{P} = \frac{3000 + 5000 + 5000 + 6000 + 4000}{5} = \frac{23000}{5} = 4600\]
  • Step 2: Calculate the average number of students enrolled in school Q.
    The enrollments for school Q are \(4000, 7000, 8000, 7000,\) and \(5000\). \[\text{Average}_{Q} = \frac{4000 + 7000 + 8000 + 7000 + 5000}{5} = \frac{31000}{5} = 6200\]
  • Step 3: Find the average of the difference between the two schools.
    The question asks for the average of the difference, which is equivalent to the difference between the two calculated averages: \[\text{Average Diff} = \text{Average}_{Q} - \text{Average}_{P} = 6200 - 4600 = 1600\]
  • Step 4: Calculate the final ratio.
    The desired ratio is the average of school P to the average of the difference: \[\text{Ratio} = \frac{4600}{1600} = \frac{46}{16} = \frac{23}{8}\]
\[\boxed{\text{B) 23 : 8} }\]

questions.question: If \(P, Q, R, S\) are four individuals, how many teams of size exceeding one can be formed, with \(Q\) as a member?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
  • Total individuals: \(\{P, Q, R, S\}\) (Total \(n = 4\)).
  • Fixed member: \(Q\) must be in every team.
  • Constraint: Team size must exceed one (Size \(> 1\)).
  • Teams of size 2: Choose 1 from \(\{P, R, S\} \Rightarrow {^3C_1} = 3\)
  • Teams of size 3: Choose 2 from \(\{P, R, S\} \Rightarrow {^3C_2} = 3\)
  • Teams of size 4: Choose 3 from \(\{P, R, S\} \Rightarrow {^3C_3} = 1\)
Total Calculation:
\[\text{Total teams} = {^3C_1} + {^3C_2} + {^3C_3} = 3 + 3 + 1 = 7\] Manual Verification (Listing Combinations):
  • Size 2: \(\{P, Q\}, \{R, Q\}, \{S, Q\}\) (3 teams)
  • Size 3: \(\{P, R, Q\}, \{P, S, Q\}, \{R, S, Q\}\) (3 teams)
  • Size 4: \(\{P, Q, R, S\}\) (1 team)
Total = \(3 + 3 + 1 = 7\). \[\boxed{\text{C) 7} }\]

questions.question: In four-digit integer numbers from 1001 to 9999, the digit group ``37'' (in the same sequence) appears ____ times.
questions.explanation:
Analysis by Position:
A four-digit number can be represented as \(d_{1}d_{2}d_{3}d_{4}\). The group "37" can occupy three possible positions:
  1. Case 1: Positions \(d_{1}d_{2}\) (37 _ _)
    • The first two digits are fixed as 37.
    • The third digit (\(d_{3}\)) can be any of the 10 digits (0-9).
    • The fourth digit (\(d_{4}\)) can be any of the 10 digits (0-9).
    • Total occurrences: \(10 \times 10 = 100\).
  2. Case 2: Positions \(d_{2}d_{3}\) (_ 37 _)
    • The middle two digits are fixed as 37.
    • The first digit (\(d_{1}\)) can be any digit from 1 to 9 (since it's a 4-digit number starting from 1001). Total = 9 choices.
    • The fourth digit (\(d_{4}\)) can be any digit from 0 to 9. Total = 10 choices.
    • Total occurrences: \(9 \times 10 = 90\).
  3. Case 3: Positions \(d_{3}d_{4}\) (_ _ 37)
    • The last two digits are fixed as 37.
    • The first digit (\(d_{1}\)) can be 1 to 9. Total = 9 choices.
    • The second digit (\(d_{2}\)) can be 0 to 9. Total = 10 choices.
    • Total occurrences: \(9 \times 10 = 90\).
Total Count:
\[\text{Total appearances} = 100 + 90 + 90 = 280\] Note on Overlap:
In the number "3737", the group "37" is counted once in Case 1 (\(d_{1}d_{2}\)) and once in Case 3 (\(d_{3}d_{4}\)). Since the question asks how many times the group appears (rather than how many numbers contain the group), this double counting is correct and required. \[\boxed{\text{C) 280} }\]

questions.question: Given a semicircle with \(O\) as the centre, as shown in the figure, the ratio \(\dfrac{\overline{AC} + \overline{CB}}{\overline{AB}}\) is ____, where \(\overline{AC}\), \(\overline{CB}\) and \(\overline{AB}\) are chords.
questions.explanation:
Given a semicircle with center \(O\). Let the radius of the circle be \(r\). Geometric Analysis:
  • \(AO = OB = OC = r\) (all are radii of the same circle).
  • \(\overline{AB}\) is the diameter, so \(AB = AO + OB = 2r\).
  • \(\triangle AOC\) and \(\triangle BOC\) are right-angled triangles because \(OC \perp AB\).
Calculating Chord Lengths:
Using the Pythagorean theorem in \(\triangle AOC\): \[AC^2 = AO^2 + OC^2 = r^2 + r^2 = 2r^2 \implies AC = \sqrt{2}r\] Similarly, in \(\triangle BOC\): \[CB^2 = BO^2 + OC^2 = r^2 + r^2 = 2r^2 \implies CB = \sqrt{2}r\] Finding the Ratio:
The required ratio is: \[\frac{AC + CB}{AB} = \frac{\sqrt{2}r + \sqrt{2}r}{2r}\] \[\frac{2\sqrt{2}r}{2r} = \sqrt{2}\] \[\boxed{{\text{B) }\sqrt{2}}}\]

If the revenue of company Q in 2015 was 20% more than that in 2014, and company Q had earned a profit of 10% on expenditure in 2014, then its expenditure (in million rupees) in 2014 was ______.
questions.explanation:

Step 2: Calculate Expenditure of Company \(Q\) in 2014
  • The problem states Company \(Q\) earned a profit of \(10\%\) in 2014.
  • Profit Formula: \(\text{Revenue} = \text{Expenditure} \times (1 + \text{Profit Percentage})\).
  • Assuming the 2010 revenue (\(37.5\)) represents the revenue for the period leading into the 2014 calculation: \[37.5 = \text{Expenditure}_{2014} \times (1 + 0.10)\] \[\text{Expenditure}_{2014} = \frac{37.5}{1.1} \approx 34.09\]
Rounding to the nearest decimal as per the options: \[\text{Expenditure} \approx 34.1\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 34.1} }\]
Key points
  • Profit Margin: Profit is calculated over the expenditure (cost). Therefore, \(\text{Revenue} = \text{Expenditure} + \text{Profit}\).
Mistakes to avoid
  • Base Value Error: Do not calculate \(10\%\) of the Revenue and subtract it. Profit is \(10\%\) of the Expenditure, so you must divide the Revenue by \(1.1\).

questions.question: The dawn of the 21st century witnessed the melting glaciers oscillating between giving too much and too little to billions of people who depend on them for fresh water. The UN climate report estimates that without deep cuts to man-made emissions, at least 30% of the northern hemisphere's surface permafrost could melt by the end of the century. Given this situation of imminent global exodus of billions of people displaced by rising seas, nation-states need to rethink their carbon footprint for political concerns, if not for environmental ones. Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage?

questions.explanation:

It also mentions a "global exodus of billions of people displaced by rising seas." This directly supports the inference that billions are affected.

questions.question: There are multiple routes to reach from node 1 to node 2, as shown in the network. The cost of travel on an edge between two nodes is given in rupees. Nodes `a', `b', `c', `d', `e', and `f' are toll booths. The toll price at toll booths marked `a' and `e' is Rs. 200, and is Rs. 100 for the other toll booths. Which is the cheapest route from node 1 to node 2?
questions.explanation:
To find the cheapest route from node 1 to node 2, we must sum the edge costs and the toll booth prices for each possible path. Toll Booth Prices:
  • Nodes 'a' and 'e' = Rs. 200 each.
  • Nodes 'b', 'c', 'd', and 'f' = Rs. 100 each.
Cost Calculation for Given Options:
  • Route A (1-a-c-2):
    Cost = (Edge \(1 \rightarrow a\)) + (Toll \(a\)) + (Edge \(a \rightarrow c\)) + (Toll \(c\)) + (Edge \(c \rightarrow 2\)) Cost = \(200 + 200 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 700\).
  • Route B (1-f-b-2):
    Cost = (Edge \(1 \rightarrow f\)) + (Toll \(f\)) + (Edge \(f \rightarrow b\)) + (Toll \(b\)) + (Edge \(b \rightarrow 2\)) Cost = \(100 + 100 + 0 + 100 + 200 = 500\).
  • Route C (1-b-2):
    Cost = (Edge \(1 \rightarrow b\)) + (Toll \(b\)) + (Edge \(b \rightarrow 2\)) Cost = \(300 + 100 + 200 = 600\).
  • Route D (1-f-e-2):
    Cost = (Edge \(1 \rightarrow f\)) + (Toll \(f\)) + (Edge \(f \rightarrow e\)) + (Toll \(e\)) + (Edge \(e \rightarrow 2\)) Cost = \(100 + 100 + 100 + 200 + 200 = 700\).
Comparing the total costs, Route B (\(500\)) is the cheapest. \[\boxed{\text{B) 1-f-b-2} }\]

questions.question: The figure below shows an annular ring with outer and inner radii as \(b\) and \(a\), respectively. The annular space has been painted in the form of blue colour circles touching the outer and inner periphery of annular space. If maximum \(n\) number of circles can be painted, then the unpainted area available in annular space is _____.
questions.explanation:
The objective is to calculate the unpainted area within an annular ring that contains \(n\) blue circles. 1. Area of the Annular Ring:
The area of an annular ring (the space between two concentric circles with radii \(a\) and \(b\), where \(b > a\)) is given by: \[\text{Area of annular ring} = \pi b^2 - \pi a^2 = \pi(b^2 - a^2)\] 2. Area of the Blue Circles:
Assuming the diameter of each blue circle fits exactly within the width of the ring, the diameter \(d = b - a\). Thus, the radius \(r\) of one blue circle is: \[r = \frac{b - a}{2}\] The area of a single blue circle is: \[\text{Area of 1 blue circle} = \pi r^2 = \pi \left( \frac{b - a}{2} \right)^2\] For \(n\) such circles, the total area is: \[\text{Area of } n \text{ blue circles} = n \pi \left( \frac{b - a}{2} \right)^2\] 3. Calculation of Unpainted Area:
The unpainted area is the difference between the total ring area and the area occupied by the blue circles: \[\text{Unpainted area} = \pi(b^2 - a^2) - n \pi \frac{(b - a)^2}{4}\] Factoring out \(\pi\): \[\text{Unpainted area} = \pi \left[ (b^2 - a^2) - \frac{n}{4}(b - a)^2 \right]\] \[\boxed{\text{A) $\pi \left[ (b^2 - a^2) - \frac{n}{4} (b - a)^2 \right]$} }\]
Key points
  • Annulus Geometry: The area is always the outer area minus the inner area: \(\pi(R_{outer}^2 - R_{inner}^2)\).
  • Linear Dimensions: Ensure the relationship between the ring's width (\(b-a\)) and the inscribed circle's diameter is correctly identified from the problem's geometry.

questions.question: Two straight lines are drawn perpendicular to each other in the \(X\)-\(Y\) plane. If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the acute angles the straight lines make with the \(X\)-axis, then \(\alpha + \beta\) is _____.
questions.explanation:
Let the two straight lines be \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), which are perpendicular to each other in the \(X\)-\(Y\) plane. Let the angle made by \(L_1\) with the positive \(X\)-axis be \(\theta_1\). Let the angle made by \(L_2\) with the positive \(X\)-axis be \(\theta_2\). Since the lines are perpendicular: \[|\theta_1 - \theta_2| = 90^\circ\] If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the acute angles these lines make with the \(X\)-axis:
  • Let \(L_1\) make an acute angle \(\alpha\) with the \(X\)-axis. Its slope \(m_1 = \tan(\alpha)\).
  • Since \(L_2 \perp L_1\), the slope of \(L_2\) is \(m_2 = -\frac{1}{m_1} = -\cot(\alpha)\).
  • We know that \(-\cot(\alpha) = \tan(90^\circ + \alpha)\). This means the angle \(L_2\) makes with the positive \(X\)-axis is \(90^\circ + \alpha\).
  • The acute angle \(\beta\) that \(L_2\) makes with the \(X\)-axis is found by taking the supplement of the obtuse angle or simply using the geometry of a right-angled triangle formed by the intersections.
In a right-angled triangle formed by the two lines and the \(X\)-axis: The interior angles of the triangle at the \(X\)-axis would be \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Since the third angle (where the lines intersect) is \(90^\circ\): \[\alpha + \beta + 90^\circ = 180^\circ\] \[\alpha + \beta = 90^\circ\] \[\boxed{\text{B) $90^\circ$} }\]
Key points
  • Perpendicular Slopes: For two lines with slopes \(m_1\) and \(m_2\), \(m_1 \cdot m_2 = -1\).
  • Acute Angle Property: The sum of two acute angles in a right-angled triangle is always \(90^\circ\) (complementary angles).

questions.question: The total revenue of a company during 2014-2018 is shown in the bar graph. If the total expenditure of the company in each year is 500 million rupees, then the aggregate profit or loss (in percentage) on the total expenditure of the company during 2014-2018 is _____.
questions.explanation:
To find the aggregate profit or loss percentage, we first need to calculate the total revenue and total expenditure for the period 2014–2018. 1. Total Expenditure:
The problem states the expenditure for each year is 500 million rupees. Total years = 5 (2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018). \[\text{Total Expenditure} = 5 \times 500 = 2500\,\text{million rupees}\] 2. Total Revenue:
Reading from the bar graph for each year:
  • 2014: 500 million
  • 2015: 700 million
  • 2016: 800 million
  • 2017: 600 million
  • 2018: 400 million
\[\text{Total Revenue} = 500 + 700 + 800 + 600 + 400 = 3000\,\text{million rupees}\] 3. Profit/Loss Calculation:
Since Total Revenue (\(3000\)) \(>\) Total Expenditure (\(2500\)), there is an aggregate profit. \[\text{Profit} = \text{Total Revenue} - \text{Total Expenditure} = 3000 - 2500 = 500\,\text{million rupees}\] 4. Profit Percentage:
The percentage is calculated on the total expenditure: \[\text{Profit \%} = \left( \frac{\text{Profit}}{\text{Total Expenditure}} \right) \times 100\] \[\text{Profit \%} = \frac{500}{2500} \times 100 = \frac{1}{5} \times 100 = 20\%\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 20 \% profit} }\]

questions.question: The sum of two positive numbers is 100. After subtracting 5 from each number, the product of the resulting numbers is 0. One of the original numbers is ______.
questions.explanation:
Let the two positive numbers be \(x\) and \(y\). From the first condition: \[x + y = 100 \implies y = 100 - x\] According to the second condition, after subtracting \(5\) from each number, their product is \(0\): \[(x - 5)(y - 5) = 0\] Substitute \(y = 100 - x\) into the equation: \[(x - 5)((100 - x) - 5) = 0\] \[(x - 5)(95 - x) = 0\] For the product to be zero, either:
  • \(x - 5 = 0 \implies x = 5\)
  • \(95 - x = 0 \implies x = 95\)
If \(x = 5\), then \(y = 100 - 5 = 95\). If \(x = 95\), then \(y = 100 - 95 = 5\). In either case, the two original numbers are \(5\) and \(95\). Checking the given options, \(95\) is listed. \[\boxed{\text{D) 95} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Insert seven numbers between 2 and 34, such that the resulting sequence including 2 and 34 is an arithmetic progression. The sum of these inserted seven numbers is______.
questions.explanation:
Identify the parameters of the Arithmetic Progression (A.P.):
  • First term (\(a\)) = \(2\)
  • Last term (\(l\) or \(t_n\)) = \(34\)
  • Number of inserted terms (\(m\)) = \(7\)
  • Total number of terms (\(n\)) = \(m + 2 = 9\)
Find the common difference (\(d\)): Using the formula \(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\): \[34 = 2 + (9 - 1)d\] \[32 = 8d\] \[d = 4\] The full sequence is: \(2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34\). The seven inserted numbers are: \(6, 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30\). Calculate the sum of these seven numbers (\(S_m\)): \[S_m = 6 + 10 + 14 + 18 + 22 + 26 + 30 = 126\] Alternatively, use the property that the sum of \(m\) arithmetic means between \(a\) and \(b\) is \(m\) times the single arithmetic mean of \(a\) and \(b\): \[S_m = m \times \left( \frac{a + b}{2} \right)\] \[S_m = 7 \times \left( \frac{2 + 34}{2} \right)\] \[S_m = 7 \times 18 = 126\] \[\boxed{\text {C) 126}}\]

questions.question: The unit's place in \(26591749^{110016}\) is ______.
questions.explanation:
Identify the base and the exponent:
  • Base: \(26591749\) (Unit's digit is \(9\))
  • Exponent: \(110016\)
Analyze the cyclicity of the unit's digit for powers of \(9\):
  • \(9^1 = 9\) (Unit's digit is \(9\))
  • \(9^2 = 81\) (Unit's digit is \(1\))
  • \(9^3 = 729\) (Unit's digit is \(9\))
  • \(9^4 = 6561\) (Unit's digit is \(1\))
From this pattern, we can conclude:
  • If the power is odd, the unit's digit is \(9\).
  • If the power is even, the unit's digit is \(1\).
Since the exponent \(110016\) is an even number, the unit's digit of \(26591749^{110016}\) must be \(1\). \[\boxed{\text{A) 1} }\]

questions.question: If \(f(x) = x^{2}\) for each \(x \in (-\infty, \infty)\), then \(\dfrac{f(f(f(x)))}{f(x)}\) is equal to ______.
questions.explanation:
Given the function: \[f(x) = x^2\] We need to find the value of the expression \(\frac{f(f(f(x)))}{f(x)}\). Step 1: Compute the composite functions
First, find \(f(f(x))\): \[f(f(x)) = f(x^2) = (x^2)^2 = x^4\] Next, find \(f(f(f(x)))\): \[f(f(f(x))) = f(x^4) = (x^4)^2 = x^8\] Step 2: Evaluate the given ratio
Substitute the results into the expression: \[\frac{f(f(f(x)))}{f(x)} = \frac{x^8}{x^2}\] Using the laws of exponents \(\frac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}\): \[\frac{x^8}{x^2} = x^{8-2} = x^6\] Step 3: Express the result in terms of \(f(x)\)
We know that \(f(x) = x^2\). We can rewrite \(x^6\) as a power of \(x^2\): \[x^6 = (x^2)^3\] Substituting \(f(x)\) back in: \[(x^2)^3 = (f(x))^3\] \[\boxed{\text {C) $(f(x))^3$}}\]

questions.question: For the year 2019, which of the previous year's calendar can be used?
questions.explanation:
To find when a calendar repeats, we calculate the cumulative number of odd days between the years. A calendar repeats when the sum of odd days is a multiple of 7 and the year type (ordinary or leap) matches. 1. Concept of Odd Days
  • Ordinary Year (365 days): \(365 \div 7 = 52\) weeks and 1 odd day.
  • Leap Year (366 days): \(366 \div 7 = 52\) weeks and 2 odd days.
2. Calculation from 2013 to 2019
We check if the calendar of 2013 repeats in 2019 by counting odd days from the start of 2013:
YearNumber of Odd Days
2013 (Ordinary)1
2014 (Ordinary)1
2015 (Ordinary)1
2016 (Leap)2
2017 (Ordinary)1
2018 (Ordinary)1
Total7
Since the total sum of odd days until the end of 2018 is 7 (which is divisible by 7), the year 2019 will begin on the same day of the week as 2013. 3. Verification of Year Type
  • 2013 is an ordinary year.
  • 2019 is an ordinary year.
Because both the starting day and the year type match, the 2013 calendar is identical to 2019. \[\boxed{\text{C) 2013} }\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The ratio of `the sum of the odd positive integers from \(1\) to \(100\)' to `the sum of the even positive integers from \(150\) to \(200\)' is ______.
questions.explanation:
We need to find the ratio of the sum of odd integers from 1 to 100 to the sum of even integers from 150 to 200. 1. Sum of odd integers from 1 to 100
The odd integers are \(1, 3, 5, \dots, 99\).
  • This is an Arithmetic Progression (AP) where \(a = 1\), \(l = 99\), and \(d = 2\).
  • Number of terms (\(n_1\)): \(\frac{99 - 1}{2} + 1 = 50\).
  • Formula for sum of first \(n\) odd numbers: \(S_{odd} = n^2\). \[S_1 = 50^2 = 2500\]
2. Sum of even integers from 150 to 200
The even integers are \(150, 152, \dots, 200\).
  • This is an AP where \(a = 150\), \(l = 200\), and \(d = 2\).
  • Number of terms (\(n_2\)): \(\frac{200 - 150}{2} + 1 = \frac{50}{2} + 1 = 26\).
  • Formula for sum of AP: \(S = \frac{n}{2}(a + l)\). \[S_2 = \frac{26}{2}(150 + 200) = 13 \times 350 = 4550\]
3. Calculating the Ratio
\[\text{Ratio} = \frac{S_1}{S_2} = \frac{2500}{4550}\] Dividing both numerator and denominator by 50: \[\frac{2500 \div 50}{4550 \div 50} = \frac{50}{91}\] The ratio is 50 : 91. \[\boxed{\text{C) 50 : 91} }\]

questions.question: In a school of \(1000\) students, \(300\) students play chess and \(600\) students play football. If \(50\) students play both chess and football, the number of students who play neither is ______.
questions.explanation:
1. Define the Sets
Let:
  • \(U\) be the universal set of all students, \(n(U) = 1000\).
  • \(C\) be the set of students who play Chess, \(n(C) = 300\).
  • \(F\) be the set of students who play Football, \(n(F) = 600\).
  • \(C \cap F\) be the set of students who play both, \(n(C \cap F) = 50\).
2. Calculate Students Playing at Least One Sport
The number of students who play either Chess or Football (or both) is given by: \[n(C \cup F) = n(C) + n(F) - n(C \cap F)\] \[n(C \cup F) = 300 + 600 - 50 = 850\] 3. Calculate Students Playing None of the Sports
The number of students who play none of the sports is the total number of students minus those who play at least one: \[\text{None} = n(U) - n(C \cup F)\] \[\text{None} = 1000 - 850 = 150\] \[\boxed{\text {B) 150}}\]

If the total number of LED bulbs sold by two firms during April--June 2018 is \(50000\), then the number of LED bulbs sold by firm \(Y\) during April--June 2018 is ______.

questions.explanation:
The problem asks for the total number of bulbs sold by firm Y from April to June given the ratios and percentage distributions. 1. Data Extraction (April–June)
  • April: Distribution = \(15\%\), Ratio \(X:Y = 3:2\)
  • May: Distribution = \(10\%\), Ratio \(X:Y = 1:4\)
  • June: Distribution = \(10\%\), Ratio \(X:Y = 9:11\)
2. Calculating Y's share for each month
  • April: \(Y = \frac{2}{3+2} \times 15\% = \frac{2}{5} \times 15\% = 6\%\)
  • May: \(Y = \frac{4}{1+4} \times 10\% = \frac{4}{5} \times 10\% = 8\%\)
  • June: \(Y = \frac{11}{9+11} \times 10\% = \frac{11}{20} \times 10\% = 5.5\%\)
3. Total Percentage and Calculation
Total percentage of bulbs sold by Y: \[\text{Total } Y\% = 6\% + 8\% + 5.5\% = 19.5\%\] Given Total bulbs sold by \(X\) and \(Y = 50,000\): \[Y = \frac{19.5}{100} \times 50,000\] \[Y = 19.5 \times 500 = 9750\] \[\boxed{\text{ MTA}}\]
